--- ppt/slides/slide1.xml
PR38 — Clinical data download & publishing
How to pull clinical data from Cloud SQL with scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py
and publish it as an immutable Pipeline V2 dataset
LUCIA repo · branch gilad/PR38
--- ppt/slides/slide2.xml
How the data flows
One command replaces the manual algo_data_download.ipynb workflow
Cloud SQL
clinical DB
(Postgres)
→
cloud-sql-proxy
local tunnel
127.0.0.1:5432
→
publish script
one query
per site
→
Local PKLs
full_<site>_<date>.pkl
+ manifest preview
→
GCS (--publish)
immutable dataset
nanose_ml/…/datasets/<id>
•  Pipeline V2 then reads the dataset by ID: dataset.dataset_id + dataset.include_sites in the run YAML
•  Files are cached to ~/.cache/lucia/datasets/<dataset_id>/ — no local pickle paths to manage
•  Without --publish nothing is uploaded: the script only extracts and validates (safe dry run)
--- ppt/slides/slide3.xml
Step 1 — Authenticate to Google Cloud
Once per session / whenever credentials expire
gcloud auth application-default login
•  Opens a browser login; sign in with your GCP-authorized Google account
•  Creates Application Default Credentials (ADC), used by both the Cloud SQL proxy and the GCS upload
•  Symptoms when this has expired:
–  proxy fails to start / authenticate
–  "Reauthentication is needed. Please run gcloud auth application-default login"
•  Plain gcloud auth login is separate — needed for gcloud storage / gsutil commands
--- ppt/slides/slide4.xml
Step 2 — Start the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy
In a separate terminal — keep it running for the whole download
cloud-sql-proxy oceanic-oxide-452908-j3:europe-west1:data --port=5432
Ready when it prints:
Listening on 127.0.0.1:5432 for oceanic-oxide-452908-j3:europe-west1:data
The proxy has started successfully and is ready for new connections!
•  Instance name format: <project-id>:<region>:<instance-name>
•  The script connects to 127.0.0.1:5432 by default (override with DB_HOST / DB_PORT)
•  "Connection refused … 127.0.0.1:5432" = the proxy is not running
--- ppt/slides/slide5.xml
Step 3 — Run the download (LUCIA)
From the lucia repo root with the project venv active
cd <path-to-your-lucia-repo> && source .venv/bin/activate
read -s -p "Database password: " DB_PASSWORD; export DB_PASSWORD
python scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py cloud-sql \
  --dataset-id clinical-multisite-2026-10-26-v1 \
  --sites BC-Site1 BC-Site2 LI-Site1 RI-Site1 \
  --output-dir ~/data/lucia \
  --query-type full            # or simple
# no --publish here: this only downloads + validates (upload = Step 4)
Orange = change for your machine.  <path-to-your-lucia-repo> is where you cloned the repo, e.g. ~/lucia or /home/<your-username>/lucia
~/  = your own home (base) folder, /home/<your-username>/. So ~/data/lucia is /home/alice/data/lucia for alice. Use echo ~ or pwd after cd ~ to see yours
•  read -s hides the password; it stays only in this shell — never in code or YAML
•  Every line except the last must end with \ — a missing \ silently drops the following flags
--- ppt/slides/slide6.xml
Step 4 — Publish
Upload the validated PKLs from Step 3 to GCS as one immutable dataset — no DB query, no proxy needed
python scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py files \
  --dataset-id clinical-multisite-2026-10-26-v1 \
  --input ~/data/lucia/full_*_2026-10-26.pkl \
  --study lucia \
  --publish
•  files mode re-validates the PKLs already on disk; --input takes every site file from that day (glob)
•  --study lucia → gs://nanose_ml/datasets_models/lucia/datasets/<id>/   ·   --study relive → …/relive/datasets/<id>/
•  Uploads immediately — no confirmation prompt (--yes is still accepted but no longer needed)
•  Success prints: Published commit manifest: gs://…/<id>/manifest.json — the pipeline can now use dataset_id: <id>
•  IDs are immutable: if it was already published, pick a new ID (e.g. …-v2)
•  Every line except the last must end with \ — otherwise --publish is dropped ("--publish: command not found")
~/ = your home folder (/home/<your-username>/) — see Step 3
--- ppt/slides/slide7.xml
Inputs explained — main arguments
Argument
Meaning
Example / default
cloud-sql
Source mode: query the clinical DB. Alternative: files (publish PKLs you already have)
cloud-sql | files
--dataset-id
Name of the immutable dataset version. Becomes the GCS folder and the value of dataset.dataset_id in pipeline configs. Cannot be reused once published
clinical-multisite-2026-10-26-v1
--sites
Space-separated site names to extract, one PKL per site. Must match site_name in the DB exactly
BC-Site1 BC-Site2 LI-Site1 RI-Site1
--output-dir
Local folder for the extracted PKLs (created if missing)
~/data/lucia
--query-type
full = all columns incl. raw/modified signal vectors (GB); simple = metadata only (MB)
full (default) | simple
--publish
Upload the validated files + manifest to GCS. Without it: validate and preview only
off
--yes
No effect — kept for old commands; --publish no longer asks for confirmation
off
--- ppt/slides/slide8.xml
Inputs explained — optional arguments & environment
Argument / variable
Meaning
Default
--snapshot-date
Date written into the file names (full_<site>_<date>.pkl)
today
--overwrite-extracts

off

Name of the env variable that holds the DB password
DB_PASSWORD
--bucket
Target GCS bucket
nanose_ml

Folder inside the bucket for datasets
datasets_models/lucia/datasets

Schema/contract version stored in the manifest
1

Where to write the local manifest preview
/tmp/lucia-datasets/<id>/manifest.json

GCP project for the storage client
from ADC

Database address (the proxy)
127.0.0.1 / 5432

clinical / postgres

### G1

**Status:** FIXED · **Verified:** yes

**Where:** `validation_only.yaml (study), src/core/config/loader.py, model_reports.py:18, 407`

ReLIVE and LUCIA shared one GCS prefix. Storage side is in (uncommitted): study: lucia | relive derives datasets_models/`<study>`/{datasets,results}. Published 2026-10-26: gs://nanose_ml/datasets_models/lucia/datasets/clinical-multisite-2026-10-26-v1 (AN-Site1, BC-Site1, BC-Site2, LI-Site1, RI-Site1; 456,876 rows) and …/relive/datasets/relive-clinical-2026-10-26-v1 (Hadasa, HTH, JEFFERSON, NAHARIA; 25,715 rows). Still open: model-report stage always builds the LUCIA report (NOT_LC/LC); it does not call build_relive_confounding_factor_report when study: relive. Historical runs were not counted by owner.

### G2

**Status:** WONTFIX · **Verified:** publish yes; scheduler no

**Where:** `scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py, notebooks/General/algo_data_download.sh`

Publish both studies every week, not by hand. One manual publish of each study is done (G1 URIs); ReLIVE site names match the DB; the "retype the dataset ID" prompt is removed. Still open: a scheduler, a new dataset ID every week (these two IDs cannot be reused), a VM service account, the Cloud SQL proxy for the job, DB_PASSWORD from Secret Manager (still hard-coded in algo_data_download.ipynb cell 4), and deleting the local pickles after publish (LUCIA ≈5.3 GB). Code uncommitted. LUCIA sites: AN-Site1, BC-Site1, BC-Site2, LI-Site1, RI-Site1. ReLIVE sites: Hadasa, HTH, JEFFERSON, NAHARIA.

### G3

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **Verified:** yes

**Where:** `configs/pipeline_v2/validation_only.yaml`

Redefine the defaults in validation_only.yaml. The current values are not the ones a run should start from: they mix tuned-model settings with notebook leftovers (H2: n_features 20, control_group L-RAD, permutations 200, blind_test_percent 0, and the tuned BRF/XGB files selected by default). The defaults file is loaded for every run (src/core/config/loader.py), so a wrong default becomes every experiment unless a run YAML overrides it. Set the defaults deliberately (groups, sensor, breath, feature count, blind-test %, selected models, permutations) and keep the alternatives in named model YAMLs, not as the base. Set the minimum number of default yaml file with a meaningful name. (should not more than 5)

### G4

**Status:** FIXED · **Verified:** yes

**Where:** `configs/pipeline_v2/grid_clean_preprocessing.yaml`

Remove configs/pipeline_v2/grid_clean_preprocessing.yaml. Nothing runs it: no .py loads it, and the only notebook reference is a commented CONFIG_PATH in notebooks/pipeline/01_preprocessing.ipynb. It is also not a valid run config on its own (no dataset or experiment; resolving it fails with dataset.dataset_id must be non-empty). Grid-clean settings already live under preprocessing.grid_clean in validation_only.yaml (disabled by default); a run that wants them should set those keys in its own run YAML. This configuration is already inside the validation only yaml.

### G5

**Status:** FIXED · **Verified:** yes

**Where:** `src/core/v2_pipeline_run.py:281, 919, src/core/config/paths.py`

Remove the features/ folder from the base run directory. Feature pickles are written under feature_runs/`<feature_run_id>`/features/. The base run still reserves `<run>`/features (v2_pipeline_run.py create_run, and paths.py artifact features_dir), which duplicates that layout. Drop it for new runs. Keep the reader fallback in resolve_feature_run so an older run that only has `<run>`/features/train_validation_set.pkl still loads.

### G6

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **Verified:** no

**Where:** `src/core/stages/training.py, src/core/train.py`

Verify train by trace in the pipeline. Patients must stay inside one split (train, validation, or test), but the model must be fit on traces (one row per trace), not collapsed to one row per patient before fitting. Confirm a finished model run: row count in the training frame matches the trace count, `trace_level_statistics_*.csv` exists, and patient-level metrics are only the aggregation after prediction.- waiting for Eran

**Status:** FIXED · **Verified:** yes

**Where:** `src/core/stages/preprocessing.py:390, src/core/stages/features.py:612-632`

Rows filtered out before feature extraction are dropped instead of being added to the estimation set. preprocessing.filters (use_feature_groups, use_feature_sensor_types, use_feature_breath_numbers, and the `include_*` lists) removes other study groups, sensor types, and breaths from data in stages/preprocessing.py (~390). The features stage then builds estimation_pickle only from what is left: valid rows not in train/test, plus invalid rows that survived. Put those filtered rows into estimation_pickle (other groups, sensors, breaths). Keep train/test and feature selection on the configured group, sensor, and breath only.

### G8- Avichai

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **Verified:** no

**Where:** `new stage after src/core/stages/training.py; input estimation_pickle.pkl`

Add an estimation pipeline based on Avichai's work. This branch only writes estimation_pickle.pkl; it never scores that set with a trained model or writes an estimation report. Add a stage after training that loads feature_runs/`<id>`/features/estimation_pickle.pkl and the model run, applies the saved models, and writes estimation outputs next to that model run. Depends on G7, so the pickle holds the rows that were filtered out rather than only train/test leftovers.

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **Verified:** no

**Where:** `configs/pipeline_v2/validation_only.yaml (training.selected_models), configs/pipeline_v2/models/`

Add different model defaults for per-trace and per-cluster, using Eran's findings. training.selected_models and `configs/pipeline_v2/models/*.yaml` are one set for every run. Clustering on trains on cluster aggregates (aggregated_signal); clustering off trains on single traces (normalized_resampled_signals). Those are different inputs and should not share hyperparameters. Ship two default model sets (per trace and per cluster) and select the set from whether clustering ran. # SW-589 — Work through the PR 38 review findings

## Context
SW-589 (assigned to you, due 2026-11-24, reporter Avichai Toubi) says: branch from current master, go through every field in "the PR 38 file", and for each one (1) validate its status, (2) fix it if needed, (3) record what changed. The task is done when every field is resolved and a PR with the updates is complete. The ticket also asks you to note ideas that would help the team work better in this repo.

"The PR 38 file" is `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`: Gilad's review of PR #38 (merge 649d87f). It has 63 findings, and each has a **Status** (ACCEPTED / WONTFIX / FIXED, or the ID of another finding) and a **Verified** value:
- **G1–G18**: Gilad's notes. 5 FIXED, 1 WONTFIX, 12 ACCEPTED. G6, G9 and G10 are waiting for Eran; G8, G11 and H5 are marked "avichai".
- **H1–H6**: High. H1–H4 point to G14, G9, G11 and G10.
- **M1–M19**: Medium, all ACCEPTED.
- **L1–L19**: Low, all ACCEPTED.
- **Questions for the author (1–5)**.

(`docs/PR38.pptx` is a separate how-to deck for `scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py`. It is not the findings list.)

## Step-by-step process

### 0. Confirm scope (before coding)
Ask Avichai two things:
- Are G8, G11 and H5 ("avichai") and G6, G9 and G10 ("waiting for Eran") yours to do, or only yours to check status on?
- Is one PR acceptable, or should the work be split into several PRs?

Default if there's no answer: one branch, with one commit per finding (or per tightly related group). Owned and blocked items get their status checked only.

### 1. Branch
`git checkout master && git pull && git checkout -b tram/SW-589-pr38-findings`
Put the Jira key in the branch name so Bitbucket links the branch to SW-589.

### 2. Add a tracking column to the file
Use the file itself as the tracker, so there is a single source of truth. In each section table (G / H / M / L), add a **Resolution** column, and under each finding add a one-line `**Resolution:**` entry giving the commit hash, the files changed, the test added, or the reason no change was needed. Update the status vocabulary under "How to read this page": keep ACCEPTED / WONTFIX / FIXED and add **BLOCKED (owner)** for items waiting on someone else.

### 3. Validation pass (read-only; covers all 63 items)
For every finding, open the `Where:` locations on current master and classify it:
- **FIXED items (G1, G4, G5, G7, G13)**: check the fix actually landed on master, since several notes say "uncommitted". Example: G4 means `configs/pipeline_v2/grid_clean_preprocessing.yaml` should be gone, but G11 still cites it. Note that G18 says the pipeline config dir is now `configs/pipeline/` and no longer `configs/pipeline_v2/`, so re-resolve every path first.
- **ACCEPTED items**: check the problem still exists on master (later merges such as #49 parallel holdouts and #50 plateau norm may have touched it). If it's already gone, mark it FIXED and cite the commit.
- **Pointer items (H1–H4)**: they follow their target finding.
- **WONTFIX (G2)**: confirm with the reporter, then leave as is.
