38	- **Avichai items (G8, G11, G19, H5):** I implement them. Use Avichai's existing work as the reference: branches such as `avichai/eran-reproduction-check` and `avichai/signal_humid_combination`. Ask him where that work lives when I need it.

41	  - G9: needs his trace-based model results (run and metric).
42	  - G6: needs a finished model run to check.

45	**Defaults** (Avichai's answer didn't cover these; change them here if he says otherwise):
46	- G19–G25 are in scope (they're in the file).
47	- The task-style items (G15–G17, G23–G25) are in scope.
48	- Several PRs split by scope (see step 7), with one commit per finding or tightly related group (see "Commit strategy" in step 4). Confirm the PR split with Avichai.

50	### 0b. Guideline: items that depend on other members' work
51	Some items use or wait on someone else's work. **Follow this process when you reach such an item while implementing a workstream.** Don't do it all up front.
52	
53	1. **Check whether their work is on master.** Run `git fetch` first, then check `origin/master`, not local branches:
54	   - Does the file or function exist? (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/master | grep <file>`)
55	   - Is it wired into the pipeline, or is it just present? (`git grep <symbol> origin/master -- src configs`)
56	   - Is there newer work on an unmerged branch? (`git log origin/master..origin/<branch>`, `git diff --stat origin/master...origin/<branch>`)
57	
58	   Record what you find, with the commit hash and date.
59	2. **If it's on master and does what the finding needs:** build on it. Cite the commit in the Resolution line.
60	3. **If it's only on an unmerged branch, or a confirmation or input is needed from the owner** (which ref is final, values such as hyperparameters, a DB procedure, agreement on a default):
61	   - **Create a Jira ticket in the SW project, assigned to that person:**
62	     - Title: `SW-589 follow-up: <ID> - <what is needed>`.
63	     - Link it to SW-589 ("relates to").
64	     - Description: the finding ID and text, what was checked on master (hash and date), the branch involved, and the exact question or input needed.
65	   - **Don't wait.** Continue with the rest of the workstream, and with any part of this item that doesn't depend on the answer.
66	   - When the answer comes, finish the item.
67	   - Never guess values that the owner has to supply.
68	4. **When reusing their code:** bring it in with `git cherry-pick -x` or `git checkout <ref> -- <file>`, so authorship and the source commit stay in history.

89	- [x] Branch `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings` created from an up-to-date master (`<owner>/<ticket>-<desc>` format).

96	- Add a **Resolution** column to each section table (G / H / M / L).

104	For every finding, open its `Where:` locations on current master and classify it.
105	
106	- **FIXED (G1, G4, G5, G7, G13):** confirm the fix actually landed on master, since several notes say "uncommitted". For example, G4 says `grid_clean_preprocessing.yaml` is removed, but G11 still cites it. Configs now live under `configs/pipeline/` (G18, G22), so re-resolve every `configs/pipeline_v2/` path.

112	  - `sub-review`, `(synthetic)` or `(real CSV)` (H4, H6, M3–M13, M15–M19): the evidence was tests in `/tmp` that aren't in the repo. Write a failing test in `tests/` that goes through the real code path.

232	### 4a. Review checkpoint after every workstream `[ ]`
233	**Rule: after I commit a workstream, I stop. I don't start the next workstream until Tram explicitly approves the current one** (e.g. "W1 approved"). Silence, or approving a different workstream, isn't approval. This also covers steps 2 and 3, which together form checkpoint **W0** (tracker columns and validation).

239	**At the end of each workstream (the checkpoint):**
240	1. All of the workstream's commits are in, and the workstream gate (4b) passes.
241	2. Tag the end with a local tag: `git tag sw589-W<n>-review`. Tags aren't pushed, so they stay local.
242	3. Write a review note at `.claude.local/reviews/review_SW-589_W<n>.md`:
243	   - **Scope:** the findings covered, and each finding's new status (FIXED / INVALID / NOT REPRODUCED / WAITING + ticket).

247	     - new and changed tests,
248	     - xfail → pass transitions,
249	     - full-suite counts before and after,

251	     - the synthetic run result.
252	   - **Metric comparison:** for workstreams that change numbers.
253	   - **Decisions I made,** and anything I wasn't sure about.

260	     - `git show <hash>` shows one finding.
261	4. Mark the workstream `[r]` (awaiting review) in this plan, then report in chat: the review note's path, a short summary, and "waiting for your approval".
262	5. **Stop.** No more code changes and no pushes until the workstream is approved.

271	  - Fix it with new commits. Don't rewrite or force-push history that has been reviewed.
272	  - Re-run the gate and move the review tag: `git tag -f sw589-W<n>-review`.
273	  - Add a "Round 2" section to the note listing only the new commits (`git diff <old review hash>..sw589-W<n>-review`), and stop again.

284	### 4b. Test and evaluation method `[ ]`
285	This builds on the repo's existing conventions: `pytest.ini` markers `unit` / `invariant` / `system` / `slow`; synthetic data only, through the `make_clinical_frame` / `clinical_pickle` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`, never real clinical files; and `xfail(strict=True)` to record confirmed defects, as SW-568 did.
286	
287	**The red → green cycle for every bug finding:**
288	1. **Reproduce (red).** Write the smallest test that shows the defect through the real code path. Use the conditions the finding names (config flags, sensor types, traces per patient). Put it in the right folder:
289	   - `tests/unit/` for one function or stage,
290	   - `tests/invariants/` for a rule that must hold for any input (patient-level splits, row conservation, determinism),
291	   - `tests/system/` for end-to-end behaviour.
292	2. **Record it.** Mark the test `xfail(strict=True, reason="SW-589 <ID>: <defect>")`. If the fix will be in a later PR, commit the test like this, so the defect is documented in the suite and the findings file links to the test.
293	3. **Fix (green).** Change the code and remove the `xfail` marker. A strict xfail that suddenly passes fails the suite, so the marker can't be forgotten.
294	4. **Check the fix is complete and doesn't break anything else:**
295	   - edge cases the finding implies (NaN, empty groups, one row per class, more than one trace per patient);
296	   - the default path, with the flag off, is unchanged;
297	   - the full suite passes.
298	5. **If the defect won't reproduce:** keep the test as a passing regression test, and mark the finding INVALID or NOT REPRODUCED (step 3).
299	
300	**What counts as proof, by type of finding:**
301	
302	| Type | Examples | Proof it's done right |
303	|---|---|---|
304	| Crash or wrong value | L9, M8, M9, M14, M19, L10 | Unit test with a known input and a hand-calculated expected output. For M14, check the sign against a case where group A is clearly higher. |
305	| Silent behaviour → explicit | L5, L6, L12, M3 | Test asserts the warning or error is raised (`pytest.warns` / `pytest.raises`), and the message names the cause. |
306	| Data leakage / split integrity | M1, H6, M2, M4, M5, G14/H1, G16 | Invariant test: no `patient_id` appears in two folds or splits; the blind-test patients aren't used before the split. Test with several rows per patient, so a row-level split visibly fails. |
307	| Rows kept, dropped or recorded | G7, G11/H3, M10, M11, L13, G12 | Row-conservation invariant: rows in = kept + dropped by recorded reason. Every drop shows in the removal audit, and the counts match. For H3, check the temperature override doesn't flip blip-rejected rows back to VALID. |
308	| Tracker / provenance | G13/G18, G14, G12 | Run a small synthetic pipeline in `tmp_path` and assert the manifest and audit workbook have the new fields (commit, branch, holdout IDs, `n_remaining_visits`). |
309	| Config contract | G22, G3, G9 | `test_pipeline_config.py`-style tests: invalid combinations are rejected at load time with a clear message; valid ones resolve to the expected values; every shipped YAML in `configs/pipeline/` still loads. |
310	| Ported work (others' code) | G10, H5, G8 | Bring their tests along (e.g. `test_eran_preprocess_path.py`). Add a parity test: same input through their original function and the wired-in stage gives the same output. |
311	| Methodology (changes numbers) | W7, W8, M12, M13, M16, M17 | Unit test of the mechanism, plus a before/after comparison (below). Agreed by Gilad and Avichai in the PR. |
312	| Report correctness | M15, M17, M18, L17, G21 | Build the report from a synthetic run where the right answer is known (e.g. 26 patients with 30 rows must report n=26), and assert the table values. G21 tests the contract in `docs/HOLDOUT_CLUSTER_CONFOUNDING_REPORT.md`. |
313	| Docs / tasks | L19, G15, G23, G25 | Every path, command and config key in the doc exists. For G15, follow the manual from a fresh clone and it runs. G23: a model rebuilt from the saved parameters produces the same predictions. |

316	- **Full suite:** `pytest` is green. Compare the counts with the baseline taken in step 5; the number of tests should only go up.
317	- **Invariants:** `pytest -m invariant` and `pytest -m system` pass.
318	- **xfails:** none of the SW-568 strict xfails changed state by accident. If one passes, that's an unexpected side effect; investigate it.
319	- **One synthetic pipeline run** through `scripts/lucia_pipeline.py`, with the stages that workstream touched, finishes without errors. For W4, run once with `grid_clean` and `blip_filter` enabled.

322	- **Same data both times:** the same published dataset ID and config, on master (before) and on the branch (after). Use fixed seeds and the same machine, so the only difference is the code.

334	- A test proves it: it failed before the fix and passes after. For tasks, the check from the table above.
335	- The full suite passes.
336	- The workstream gate passes.

364	One PR with all 69 findings would mix safe fixes with changes that move model metrics. It would be too large to review, and one disputed change (e.g. G3 defaults) would hold up everything else. It would also need every reviewer (Gilad, Eran, Avichai) to read all of it. Splitting by scope lets safe work merge first and sends each PR to the people who know that code.

# Plan: SW-589, work through the PR 38 review findings (v1)

- **Jira:** SW-589, "Implement changes from 'PR 38' file" (In Progress, due 2026-11-24, reporter Avichai Toubi)

## How this plan is used
- This file is the source of truth for the task. Claude implements only what the plan says.

1. Validate its status.
2. Fix it if needed.
3. Record what changed.

The task is done when every item is resolved and a PR with the updates is complete. The ticket also asks for ideas that would help the team work better in this repo.

"The PR 38 file" is `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`. Commit `de32631` turned it into a "Full review of the model pipeline" and added G19–G25. Existing statuses didn't change. It now has **69 findings** plus **5 questions for the author**:

| Group | Items | Status breakdown |

### 4. Fix pass, by workstream `[ ]`
Related findings touch the same code, so they're fixed together. Work through the workstreams in order: the low-risk ones come first, and the ones that change model numbers or depend on others come last. Each fix needs a test that fails before the change (when it's a bug).

#### Commit strategy
Two levels: **the workstream decides which branch and PR a commit goes into; the finding decides what goes into one commit.**

- **One commit per finding**, or per pointer group fixed together (e.g. G11 + H3, G13 + G18, M1 + H6). Each commit holds:
  - the code change,
  - the test that proves it,
  - that finding's Status and Resolution row in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`.

  The finding, its proof and its tracker update then land together and can be reverted together.
- **Never mix workstreams in one commit.** A commit belongs to exactly one workstream, so a workstream can move to a different PR without rewriting commits.
- **No single squashed commit per workstream.** It would hide which change fixed which finding and make `git bisect` useless when a metric moves. The workstream is still visible as a unit: its commits sit together in the history, and its PR is what reviewers see.
- **Per-workstream commits are allowed only for shared groundwork**, e.g. one "add test fixtures for preprocessing" commit at the start of W4, used by later finding commits.
- **Housekeeping commits are separate from behavior commits:**
  - the `.gitignore` change,
  - the step 2 tracker columns,
  - the step 3 validation table,
  - doc-only fixes.
- **Before every commit:** `pytest` passes, the diff contains only that finding's files, and nothing from `.claude.local/`, data, PKLs or notebook outputs.
- **Message format:** `SW-589 <ID>: <imperative summary>`, e.g. `SW-589 M19: Stop the loop variable shadowing prevalence`. The `SW-589` key lets Bitbucket link the commit to Jira. The body says what was wrong, what changed, and how it was tested. **No co-author or "Generated with" attribution lines** (Tram's rule).
- **Commit order:** the order of the workstream list, so each commit builds on fixed inputs.

### 4b. Test and evaluation method `[ ]`
This builds on the repo's existing conventions: `pytest.ini` markers `unit` / `invariant` / `system` / `slow`; synthetic data only, through the `make_clinical_frame` / `clinical_pickle` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`, never real clinical files; and `xfail(strict=True)` to record confirmed defects, as SW-568 did.

**The red → green cycle for every bug finding:**
1. **Reproduce (red).** Write the smallest test that shows the defect through the real code path. Use the conditions the finding names (config flags, sensor types, traces per patient). Put it in the right folder:
   - `tests/unit/` for one function or stage,
   - `tests/invariants/` for a rule that must hold for any input (patient-level splits, row conservation, determinism),
   - `tests/system/` for end-to-end behaviour.
2. **Record it.** Mark the test `xfail(strict=True, reason="SW-589 <ID>: <defect>")`. If the fix will be in a later PR, commit the test like this, so the defect is documented in the suite and the findings file links to the test.
3. **Fix (green).** Change the code and remove the `xfail` marker. A strict xfail that suddenly passes fails the suite, so the marker can't be forgotten.
4. **Check the fix is complete and doesn't break anything else:**
   - edge cases the finding implies (NaN, empty groups, one row per class, more than one trace per patient);
   - the default path, with the flag off, is unchanged;
   - the full suite passes.
5. **If the defect won't reproduce:** keep the test as a passing regression test, and mark the finding INVALID or NOT REPRODUCED (step 3).

**What counts as proof, by type of finding:**

| Type | Examples | Proof it's done right |
|---|---|---|
| Crash or wrong value | L9, M8, M9, M14, M19, L10 | Unit test with a known input and a hand-calculated expected output. For M14, check the sign against a case where group A is clearly higher. |
| Silent behaviour → explicit | L5, L6, L12, M3 | Test asserts the warning or error is raised (`pytest.warns` / `pytest.raises`), and the message names the cause. |
| Data leakage / split integrity | M1, H6, M2, M4, M5, G14/H1, G16 | Invariant test: no `patient_id` appears in two folds or splits; the blind-test patients aren't used before the split. Test with several rows per patient, so a row-level split visibly fails. |
| Rows kept, dropped or recorded | G7, G11/H3, M10, M11, L13, G12 | Row-conservation invariant: rows in = kept + dropped by recorded reason. Every drop shows in the removal audit, and the counts match. For H3, check the temperature override doesn't flip blip-rejected rows back to VALID. |
| Tracker / provenance | G13/G18, G14, G12 | Run a small synthetic pipeline in `tmp_path` and assert the manifest and audit workbook have the new fields (commit, branch, holdout IDs, `n_remaining_visits`). |
| Config contract | G22, G3, G9 | `test_pipeline_config.py`-style tests: invalid combinations are rejected at load time with a clear message; valid ones resolve to the expected values; every shipped YAML in `configs/pipeline/` still loads. |
| Ported work (others' code) | G10, H5, G8 | Bring their tests along (e.g. `test_eran_preprocess_path.py`). Add a parity test: same input through their original function and the wired-in stage gives the same output. |
| Methodology (changes numbers) | W7, W8, M12, M13, M16, M17 | Unit test of the mechanism, plus a before/after comparison (below). Agreed by Gilad and Avichai in the PR. |
| Report correctness | M15, M17, M18, L17, G21 | Build the report from a synthetic run where the right answer is known (e.g. 26 patients with 30 rows must report n=26), and assert the table values. G21 tests the contract in `docs/HOLDOUT_CLUSTER_CONFOUNDING_REPORT.md`. |
| Docs / tasks | L19, G15, G23, G25 | Every path, command and config key in the doc exists. For G15, follow the manual from a fresh clone and it runs. G23: a model rebuilt from the saved parameters produces the same predictions. |

**Workstream gate** (must pass before the workstream counts as done):
- **Full suite:** `pytest` is green. Compare the counts with the baseline taken in step 5; the number of tests should only go up.
- **Invariants:** `pytest -m invariant` and `pytest -m system` pass.
- **xfails:** none of the SW-568 strict xfails changed state by accident. If one passes, that's an unexpected side effect; investigate it.
- **One synthetic pipeline run** through `scripts/lucia_pipeline.py`, with the stages that workstream touched, finishes without errors. For W4, run once with `grid_clean` and `blip_filter` enabled.

### 7. Pull requests and ticket `[ ]`
**Decision: several PRs, split by how risky the changes are. Not one combined PR.**

One PR with all 69 findings would mix safe fixes with changes that move model metrics. It would be too large to review, and one disputed change (e.g. G3 defaults) would hold up everything else. **Rules:**
- **Merge in order (PR 1 → 5).** Each later branch is cut from master after the previous PR merges (or rebased onto it). Every PR edits `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`, so merging in order keeps conflicts small, and each PR is tested on fixed inputs.
- **No stacked PRs open at once,** except PR 4 (reports), which only depends on PR 1 and can run alongside PR 2 and PR 3 if time is tight.

"""Raw-derivative UP/DOWN landmark detection for GRID_CLEAN preprocessing.

Each sensor trace is handled independently. A candidate is three consecutive raw
derivatives past the sensor threshold. It is rejected only when both following
derivatives reverse by at least half that threshold.

Search order is fixed: DB ±15, allowed device stages, DB ±150, then the original
DB landmark. UP and DOWN fall back independently.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

FIXED_UP_THRESHOLDS: dict[str, float] = {
    "type_1": 130.0,
    "type_2": 130.0,
    "type_7": 65.0,
    "type_8": 65.0,
}
FIXED_DOWN_THRESHOLDS: dict[str, float] = {
    "type_1": 65.0,
    "type_2": 70.0,
    "type_7": 35.0,
    "type_8": 35.0,
}

UP_ALLOWED_STEPS: tuple[int, ...] = (2, 3, 4)
DOWN_ALLOWED_STEPS: tuple[int, ...] = (4, 5, 6)
DB_CLOSE_WINDOW = 15
DB_WIDE_WINDOW = 150
EXAM_KEYS = ("patient_id", "unit_id", "usage_number")

TRIGGER_DETECTION_CFG: dict[str, Any] = {
    "up_thresholds": FIXED_UP_THRESHOLDS,
    "down_thresholds": FIXED_DOWN_THRESHOLDS,
    "close_window": DB_CLOSE_WINDOW,
    "wide_window": DB_WIDE_WINDOW,
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Landmark:
    """One landmark result, including which funnel stage supplied it."""

    index: int
    ok: bool
    source: str
    threshold: float


def step_span(steps: Any, allowed: Sequence[int]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """Return the inclusive sample span occupied by the allowed device stages."""
    try:
        values = np.asarray(steps, dtype=float).ravel()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    indices = np.flatnonzero(np.isin(values, list(allowed)))
    return (int(indices[0]), int(indices[-1])) if indices.size else None


def find_landmark(
    signal: Any,
    *,
    rising: bool,
    threshold: float,
    search_from: int = 0,
    search_to: int | None = None,
) -> Landmark:
    """Find the first three-step transition without a two-step strong reversal.

    ``index`` is the approved plotted landmark. UP returns the sample immediately
    before the three qualifying rises. DOWN returns the first sample after the
    first qualifying drop.
    """
    derivative = np.diff(np.asarray(signal, dtype=float).ravel())
    threshold = abs(float(threshold))
    lo = max(0, int(search_from))
    hi = min(
        derivative.size,
        derivative.size if search_to is None else max(0, int(search_to)),
    )

    # Five derivatives are needed: three triggers and two reversal checks.
    for index in range(lo, max(lo, hi - 4)):
        trigger = derivative[index : index + 3]
        following = derivative[index + 3 : index + 5]
        strong = np.all(trigger >= threshold) if rising else np.all(trigger <= -threshold)
        reversed_twice = (
            np.all(following <= -threshold / 2)
            if rising
            else np.all(following >= threshold / 2)
        )
        if strong and not reversed_twice:
            # diff[index] is signal[index + 1] - signal[index]. The DOWN
            # first-descent sample is therefore index + 1; UP intentionally
            # keeps the pre-rise sample used by the established geometry.
            landmark_index = index if rising else index + 1
            return Landmark(landmark_index, True, "detected", threshold)

    return Landmark(-1, False, "unresolved", threshold)


def find_with_db_priority(
    signal: Any,
    *,
    rising: bool,
    threshold: float,
    stage_span: tuple[int, int] | None,
    db_landmark: int,
    close_window: int = DB_CLOSE_WINDOW,
    wide_window: int = DB_WIDE_WINDOW,
) -> Landmark:
    """Search DB-close, stages, DB-wide, then preserve the DB landmark."""
    searches: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = [
        ("db_close", db_landmark - close_window, db_landmark + close_window),
    ]
    if stage_span is not None:
        searches.append(("stages", stage_span[0], stage_span[1] + 1))
    searches.append(("db_wide", db_landmark - wide_window, db_landmark + wide_window))

    for source, start, stop in searches:
        found = find_landmark(
            signal,
            rising=rising,
            threshold=threshold,
            search_from=start,
            search_to=stop,
        )
        if found.ok:
            return Landmark(found.index, True, source, found.threshold)
    return Landmark(int(db_landmark), False, "db", threshold)


def _finite_index(value: Any) -> int | None:
    """DB sample index, or None when the landmark is missing."""
    number = pd.to_numeric(value, errors="coerce")
    if pd.isna(number):
        return None
    return int(number)


def _finite_tuple(value: Any) -> np.ndarray | None:
    """Section-tuple endpoints, or None when any endpoint is missing."""
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)):
        return None
    try:
        anchors = np.asarray(value, dtype=float).ravel()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if anchors.size == 0 or not np.isfinite(anchors).all():
        return None
    return anchors.astype(int)


def _detect_row(
    row: pd.Series,

"""Raw-derivative UP/DOWN landmark detection for GRID_CLEAN preprocessing.

Each sensor trace is handled independently. A candidate is three consecutive raw
derivatives past the sensor threshold. It is rejected only when both following
derivatives reverse by at least half that threshold.

Search order is fixed: DB ±15, allowed device stages, DB ±150, then the original
DB landmark. UP and DOWN fall back independently.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

FIXED_UP_THRESHOLDS: dict[str, float] = {
    "type_1": 130.0,
    "type_2": 130.0,
    "type_7": 65.0,
    "type_8": 65.0,
}
FIXED_DOWN_THRESHOLDS: dict[str, float] = {
    "type_1": 65.0,
    "type_2": 70.0,
    "type_7": 35.0,
    "type_8": 35.0,
}

UP_ALLOWED_STEPS: tuple[int, ...] = (2, 3, 4)
DOWN_ALLOWED_STEPS: tuple[int, ...] = (4, 5, 6)
DB_CLOSE_WINDOW = 15
DB_WIDE_WINDOW = 150
EXAM_KEYS = ("patient_id", "unit_id", "usage_number")

TRIGGER_DETECTION_CFG: dict[str, Any] = {
    "up_thresholds": FIXED_UP_THRESHOLDS,
    "down_thresholds": FIXED_DOWN_THRESHOLDS,
    "close_window": DB_CLOSE_WINDOW,
    "wide_window": DB_WIDE_WINDOW,
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Landmark:
    """One landmark result, including which funnel stage supplied it."""

    index: int
    ok: bool
    source: str
    threshold: float


def step_span(steps: Any, allowed: Sequence[int]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """Return the inclusive sample span occupied by the allowed device stages."""
    try:
        values = np.asarray(steps, dtype=float).ravel()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    indices = np.flatnonzero(np.isin(values, list(allowed)))
    return (int(indices[0]), int(indices[-1])) if indices.size else None


def find_landmark(
    signal: Any,
    *,
    rising: bool,
    threshold: float,
    search_from: int = 0,
    search_to: int | None = None,
) -> Landmark:
    """Find the first three-step transition without a two-step strong reversal.

    ``index`` is the approved plotted landmark. UP returns the sample immediately
    before the three qualifying rises. DOWN returns the first sample after the
    first qualifying drop.
    """
    derivative = np.diff(np.asarray(signal, dtype=float).ravel())
    threshold = abs(float(threshold))
    lo = max(0, int(search_from))
    hi = min(
        derivative.size,
        derivative.size if search_to is None else max(0, int(search_to)),
    )

    # Five derivatives are needed: three triggers and two reversal checks.
    for index in range(lo, max(lo, hi - 4)):
        trigger = derivative[index : index + 3]
        following = derivative[index + 3 : index + 5]
        strong = np.all(trigger >= threshold) if rising else np.all(trigger <= -threshold)
        reversed_twice = (
            np.all(following <= -threshold / 2)
            if rising
            else np.all(following >= threshold / 2)
        )
        if strong and not reversed_twice:
            # diff[index] is signal[index + 1] - signal[index]. The DOWN
            # first-descent sample is therefore index + 1; UP intentionally
            # keeps the pre-rise sample used by the established geometry.
            landmark_index = index if rising else index + 1
            return Landmark(landmark_index, True, "detected", threshold)

    return Landmark(-1, False, "unresolved", threshold)


def find_with_db_priority(
    signal: Any,
    *,
    rising: bool,
    threshold: float,
    stage_span: tuple[int, int] | None,
    db_landmark: int,
    close_window: int = DB_CLOSE_WINDOW,
    wide_window: int = DB_WIDE_WINDOW,
) -> Landmark:
    """Search DB-close, stages, DB-wide, then preserve the DB landmark."""
    searches: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = [
        ("db_close", db_landmark - close_window, db_landmark + close_window),
    ]
    if stage_span is not None:
        searches.append(("stages", stage_span[0], stage_span[1] + 1))
    searches.append(("db_wide", db_landmark - wide_window, db_landmark + wide_window))

    for source, start, stop in searches:
        found = find_landmark(
            signal,
            rising=rising,
            threshold=threshold,
            search_from=start,
            search_to=stop,
        )
        if found.ok:
            return Landmark(found.index, True, source, found.threshold)
    return Landmark(int(db_landmark), False, "db", threshold)


def _finite_index(value: Any) -> int | None:
    """DB sample index, or None when the landmark is missing."""
    number = pd.to_numeric(value, errors="coerce")
    if pd.isna(number):
        return None
    return int(number)


def _finite_tuple(value: Any) -> np.ndarray | None:
    """Section-tuple endpoints, or None when any endpoint is missing."""
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)):
        return None
    try:
        anchors = np.asarray(value, dtype=float).ravel()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if anchors.size == 0 or not np.isfinite(anchors).all():
        return None
    return anchors.astype(int)


def _detect_row(
    row: pd.Series,
    *,
    signal_col: str,
    sensor_type_col: str,
    step_col: str,
    up_db_col: str,
    down_db_col: str,
    up_thresholds: dict[str, float],
    down_thresholds: dict[str, float],
    close_window: int,
    wide_window: int,
) -> tuple[Landmark, Landmark]:
    signal = row[signal_col]
    sensor_type = str(row.get(sensor_type_col))
    up_db = _finite_index(row[up_db_col])
    down_db = _finite_index(row[down_db_col])
    steps = row.get(step_col)

    def one(rising: bool) -> Landmark:
        thresholds = up_thresholds if rising else down_thresholds
        threshold = thresholds.get(sensor_type)
        db = up_db if rising else down_db
        if db is None:
            return Landmark(-1, False, "missing_db", 0.0)
        if threshold is None:
            return Landmark(db, False, "db_unsupported_sensor_type", 0.0)
        allowed = UP_ALLOWED_STEPS if rising else DOWN_ALLOWED_STEPS
        return find_with_db_priority(
            signal,
            rising=rising,
            threshold=threshold,
            stage_span=step_span(steps, allowed),
            db_landmark=db,
            close_window=close_window,
            wide_window=wide_window,
        )

    return one(True), one(False)

    """Detect UP and DOWN per row and return diagnostics without changing inputs."""
    required = (signal_col, up_db_col, down_db_col)

    if missing:

    ]
    up = [pair[0] for pair in pairs]

"""
Unified sensor fusion API.

Skips fusion when only one sensor type is present.

The late / early / autoencoder / leak_free implementations lived in
``src.core.archive`` and were dropped with the rest of the legacy tree, so only
``none`` is available. Selecting any other mode raises rather than silently
returning unfused data.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

FUSION_MODES = ("none",)
REMOVED_FUSION_MODES = ("late", "early", "autoencoder", "leak_free")


def should_run_fusion(sensor_types: list[str], cluster_enabled: bool) -> bool:
    return cluster_enabled and len(sensor_types) > 1


def apply_sensor_fusion(
    data: pd.DataFrame,
    sensor_types: list[str],
    mode: str = "late",
    cluster_enabled: bool = True,
    target_column: str = "Binary_Study_Group",
    signal_column: str = "normalized_resampled_signals",
    patient_column: str = "Patient_Id",
    n_features: int = 20,
    selection_method: str = "ensemble",
    increase_buffer: int = 30,
    recovery_buffer: int = 50,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame | None]:
    """
    Apply sensor fusion if preconditions met; otherwise return data unchanged.

    Fusion requires per-breath clustering (cluster_enabled=True) and multiple sensor types.
    """
    mode = mode.lower()
    if mode == "none" or not should_run_fusion(sensor_types, cluster_enabled):
        _logger.info(
            "Skipping sensor fusion: mode=%s, sensor_types=%s, cluster_enabled=%s",
            mode,
            sensor_types,
            cluster_enabled,
        )
        return data, None

    if mode in REMOVED_FUSION_MODES:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"Fusion mode {mode!r} was implemented in src.core.archive, which is no "
            f"longer part of this tree. Available modes: {FUSION_MODES}"
        )

    raise ValueError(f"Unknown fusion mode: {mode}. Choose from {FUSION_MODES}")

class ThresholdClassifier(BaseEstimator, ClassifierMixin):
    """Duplicate of src.core.training.ThresholdClassifier"""
    base_estimator: BaseEstimator
    cv_folds: int = 5
    threshold_metric: str = "balanced_accuracy"  # "balanced_accuracy" | "youden" | "f1"
    min_sensitivity: float = 0.0                 # optional constraint
    min_specificity: float = 0.0                 # optional constraint
    min_pos_rate: float = 0.0                    # optional constraint on positive rate
    threshold_: Optional[float] = None

    def _score_at_threshold(self, y, scores, t):
        preds = (scores >= t).astype(int)
        tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, preds).ravel()
        sens = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0
        spec = tn / (tn + fp) if (tn + fp) else 0.0

        # constraints
        if sens < self.min_sensitivity or spec < self.min_specificity:
            return -np.inf, sens, spec

        if self.threshold_metric == "balanced_accuracy":
            return 0.5 * (sens + spec), sens, spec
        elif self.threshold_metric == "youden":
            return sens + spec - 1.0, sens, spec
        elif self.threshold_metric == "f1":
            # compute F1 via PR at this single threshold
            prec = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
            f1 = (2 * prec * sens) / (prec + sens + 1e-12)
            return f1, sens, spec
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown threshold_metric: {self.threshold_metric}")

    def fit(self, X, y, groups):
        """``groups`` (patient ids) keeps every row of a patient in one OOF fold.

        A patient has several rows (several fwts in cluster mode, several
        device channels per fwt in trace mode); the threshold must not be
        tuned on rows whose siblings were in the fold's training part.
        """
        # 1) Out-of-fold scores on the TRAIN set
        classes, class_counts = np.unique(y, return_counts=True)
        if len(classes) != 2:
            # Tiny OOF folds can lose one arm when validation holds out the
            # only positive patient (Batch-2 2×0+1×200 train).
            self.threshold_ = 0.5
            self.base_estimator_ = DummyClassifier(
                strategy="constant", constant=int(classes[0])
            ).fit(X, y)
            return self
        groups = np.asarray(groups)
        if len(groups) != len(y):
            raise ValueError(f"groups has {len(groups)} rows, y has {len(y)}")
        n_groups_per_class = min(len(np.unique(groups[y == c])) for c in classes)
        n_splits = min(int(self.cv_folds), n_groups_per_class)
        if n_splits < 2:
            self.threshold_ = 0.5
            self.base_estimator_ = clone(self.base_estimator).fit(X, y)
            return self
        sgkf = StratifiedGroupKFold(
            n_splits=n_splits,
            shuffle=True,
            random_state=42,
        )
        oof = np.zeros_like(y, dtype=float)
        for tr, va in sgkf.split(X, y, groups):
            m = clone(self.base_estimator)
            m.fit(X[tr], y[tr])
            proba = m.predict_proba(X[va])
            if proba.shape[1] == 1:
                only = int(m.classes_[0])
                oof[va] = proba[:, 0] if only == 1 else 0.0
            else:
                oof[va] = proba[:, 1]

        # 2) Candidate thresholds `thr` (THIS is what was missing)
        # Use quantiles of the OOF scores to keep search compact + endpoints
        thr = np.unique(np.quantile(oof, np.linspace(0, 1, 201)))
        thr = np.clip(thr, 0.0, 1.0)
        # Ensure we also evaluate 0.0 and 1.0 explicitly
        thr = np.unique(np.concatenate(([0.0], thr, [1.0])))

        # Optional positive-rate constraint: drop thresholds violating it
        if self.min_pos_rate > 0:
            pos_rate = [(oof >= t).mean() for t in thr]
            thr = np.array([t for t, r in zip(thr, pos_rate) if r >= self.min_pos_rate])
            if thr.size == 0:  # fallback if all filtered
                thr = np.unique(np.concatenate(([0.0], np.quantile(oof, np.linspace(0, 1, 201)), [1.0])))

        # 3) Pick best threshold
        best_score, best_thr = -np.inf, 0.5
        for t in thr:
            score, sens, spec = self._score_at_threshold(y, oof, t)
            if score > best_score:
                best_score, best_thr = score, float(t)

        self.threshold_ = best_thr
        # No candidate met min_sensitivity/min_specificity: best_thr is the
        # untouched 0.5 default, i.e. the model is effectively untuned.
        self.threshold_fallback_ = bool(best_score == -np.inf)

        # 4) Fit final estimator on full TRAIN data
        self.base_estimator_ = clone(self.base_estimator).fit(X, y)
        return self

    def predict_proba(self, X):
        proba = self.base_estimator_.predict_proba(X)
        if proba.shape[1] == 2:
            return proba
        only = int(self.base_estimator_.classes_[0])
        out = np.zeros((len(proba), 2), dtype=float)
        if only in (0, 1):
            out[:, only] = proba[:, 0]
        else:
            out[:, 1] = proba[:, 0]
        return out

    def predict(self, X):
        proba = self.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]

)

    "random": (
        "Independent draw every permutation. Simple and unbiased on average, "
        "but per-patient validation counts follow a binomial spread, so some "
        "patients are validated far more often than others."
    ),
    "balanced_sites": (
        "Independent draw every permutation, stratified by site so each "
        "site's share of the validation set matches its share of that group's "
        "pool. Fixes site representativeness; does not even out per-patient "
        "coverage."
    ),
    "balanced_coverage": (
        "Draws from a per-group bag without replacement, refilling only once "
        "the bag empties. A patient cannot enter round k+1 before every "
        "patient in its group has been used in round k, which bounds the "
        "spread of per-patient validation counts to one. Site mix is left to "
        "chance."
    ),
    "balanced_sites_coverage": (
        "Bag-without-replacement drawn per (group, site) using the same site "
        "quotas as balanced_sites. Evens out per-patient coverage and holds "
        "the site mix at the same time."
    ),
    "rotating": (
        "Splits each group into disjoint slices sized by the validation "
        "proportion and walks them in order, reshuffling after a full cycle. "


class RandomDrawer(ValidationDrawer):
    method = "random"

    def __init__(
        self,
        valid_patients: Mapping[Any, Sequence[Any]],
        val_fraction: float,
        groups: Sequence[Any],
        rng: Any = random,
    ) -> None:
        self._pools = {grp: list(valid_patients[grp]) for grp in groups}
        self._fraction = val_fraction
        self._rng = rng

    def draw(self) -> Dict[Any, List[Any]]:
        return {

"""SW-589 L1, L2: validation draw sizes match what the code and docs claim."""
import random
import warnings

import pytest

from src.core.partition_testing import RotatingDrawer, _n_to_draw


def _legacy_n_val(pool_size: int, val_size: float) -> int:
    """The pre-Pipeline-V2 count (train._select_validation_patients_by_percent)."""
    n_val = max(1, round(pool_size * val_size / 100.0))
    return min(n_val, pool_size - 1)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("val_size", [20, 11.1111])
def test_random_draw_size_matches_legacy_for_shipped_val_sizes(val_size):
    """L1: the comment in train.py claims the random draw reproduces old runs.

    That holds for the val_size values the shipped configs use, for pools of
    2+ patients. These are the cases the comment now names.
    """
    for pool_size in range(2, 2000):
        assert _n_to_draw(pool_size, val_size / 100.0) == _legacy_n_val(pool_size, val_size)


def test_random_draw_size_differs_from_legacy_where_the_comment_says():
    """L1: the documented exceptions are real (35% of 90; a one-patient pool)."""
    assert _n_to_draw(90, 35 / 100.0) == 31
    assert _legacy_n_val(90, 35) == 32
    assert _n_to_draw(1, 0.2) == 1
    assert _legacy_n_val(1, 20) == 0


def _pools(n=30):
    return {0: [f"a{i}" for i in range(n)], 1: [f"b{i}" for i in range(n)]}


def test_rotating_warns_when_slices_cannot_match_the_proportion():
    """L2: 30% gives 3 slices, i.e. 33% per slice; this used to happen silently."""

        drawer = RotatingDrawer(_pools(), 0.30, (0, 1), rng=random.Random(0))

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)
        drawer = RotatingDrawer(_pools(), 0.20, (0, 1), rng=random.Random(0))

    assert drawer.n_slices == 5
    assert drawer.effective_fraction == pytest.approx(0.20)

content.content:
`down_anchor: last_plateau` moves only the DOWN window one sample earlier;
`down_anchor: one_before_last_plateau` moves it two samples earlier.

## Blip exclusion

The blip rule is outside GRID_CLEAN preprocessing and therefore applies equally to
GRID_CLEAN and Gilad paths. A trace is retained only when:

- corrections strictly before DOWN are at most 9;
- corrections strictly after DOWN are at most 4;
- total corrections in the recorded window are at most 12.

`type_5` is exempt from this rule. The exemption does not bypass unrelated
validity filters.

## Configuration

The standalone preprocessing profile is
`configs/experiments/pipeline_lucia_grid_clean_preprocess.yaml`.

Important switches:

- `filter.override_blip.enabled`: apply the shared blip rule.
- `process.grid_clean_preprocess`: choose GRID_CLEAN for supported types.
- `process.down_anchor`: `first_descent`, `last_plateau`, or
  `one_before_last_plateau`.
- `process.plateau_alignment_method`: `crop_pad` (default) or `cubic`.

In pipeline-v2 configs the same geometry lives under
`preprocessing.grid_clean`, which adds an optional length gate:

- `plateau_middle_target`: the middle-plateau length to cut to. Null, the
  default, derives it from the cohort.
- `plateau_length_tolerance`: null by default, which skips the gate. When both
  are set, a cut signal is kept only if its length lands inside
  `target_len +- tolerance`, where `target_len = plateau_before_up +
  plateau_middle_target + plateau_after_down_start`.

The gate drops traces rather than clipping them, so an exam whose breath is far
longer than the cohort can lose every trace and disappear from the run. That is
intended - such a breath would otherwise be aligned against a window it never
filled - but it means the scored cohort can be smaller than the loaded one.

The detector thresholds, derivative rule, State spans, and search funnel are
fixed in `src/core/trigger_detection.py`; legacy trigger configuration keys are
discarded. OOF, TSF, cohort selection, feature selection, and classifier
settings are deliberately absent until those paths are part of the production
pipeline.

`load.channel_type_filter` must be null so the State channel reaches GRID_CLEAN
preprocessing. `filter.sensor_types` remains a cohort-selection filter; it does
not define routing support.

## Main functions

`trigger_detection.find_landmark`
: Applies the raw three-step and reversal rule inside one search interval.

`trigger_detection.find_with_db_priority`
: Runs the close DB, State, wide DB, and DB-fallback funnel for one landmark.

`trigger_detection.detect_frame`
: Detects UP and DOWN independently for every sensor trace and records sources
  and thresholds.

`trigger_detection.apply_new_landmarks`
: Preserves DB landmarks, writes detected scalar landmarks, and re-anchors the
  section tuples independently.

`grid_clean_preprocess.prepare_grid_clean_plateau_df`
: Materializes the canonical raw/modified signal choice into `RAWData`.

`grid_clean_preprocess.attach_device_steps`
: Copies each exam's State channel onto its sensor rows.

`grid_clean_preprocess.map_db_frame_to_corrected`
: Keeps State, DB landmarks, and section tuples in one coordinate frame for
  shortened corrected signals.

`grid_clean_preprocess.apply_grid_clean_median_filter`
: Measures the cohort median UP-to-DOWN duration, applies the asymmetric length
  gate, and derives the alignment layout.

`grid_clean_preprocess.run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization`
: Runs detection, median filtering, plateau alignment, z-score, and output
  guards in the required order.

`grid_clean_preprocess.preprocess_dataframe_grid_clean`
: Public entry point called by the preprocessing stage
  (`src/core/stages/preprocessing.py`).

## Deliberately separate follow-ups

The current change does not alter validated alignment or normalization.
Potential later work should be measured independently:

- fit and persist the median alignment target instead of deriving it from every
  inference batch;
- replace proportional coordinate mapping if the correction engine exposes an
  exact raw-to-corrected index map;
- vectorize DataFrame row loops only if profiling shows they are material.

preprocessing:
  channel_type_filter:
  before_up_trig: 60
  after_down_trig: 120
  alignment_strategy: fixed
  signal_length_range: [450, 700]
  fixed_target_length: 482
  normalization_method: l2
  normalization_signal_column: resampled_signals
  # Cohort-specific site/unit/breath overrides are opt-in.
  apply_overrides: false
  override_remove_matching: false
  upload_audit: true
  audit_filename: example_removal_audit.xlsx
  blip_filter:
    enabled: false
    max_pre_down: 9
    max_post_down: 4
    max_total: 12
    exempt_sensor_types: [type_5]
    count_down_trig_sample: true
  # Optional cohort-derived plateau alignment and derivative trigger path.
  grid_clean:
    enabled: false
    plateau_before_up: 30
    plateau_after_down_start: 90
    up_feature_length: 45
    down_feature_length: 60
    # first_descent | last_plateau | one_before_last_plateau
    down_anchor: last_plateau
    use_breath_median_for_alignment: true
    plateau_median_global: true
    median_from_up_start_to_down_start: true
    plateau_median_tolerance_below: 60
    plateau_median_tolerance_above: 90
    plateau_alignment_method: crop_pad
    smooth_mid: false
    smooth_all: false
    smooth_all_except: false
    plateau_savgol_window: 5
    plateau_savgol_poly: 2
    # Both only take effect with the median gate above turned off: while
    # use_breath_median_for_alignment and plateau_median_global are set, the
    # cohort median overwrites plateau_middle_target and clears the tolerance
    # in favour of the asymmetric -60 / +90 window. With the gate off, these
    # two pin the layout instead, cutting to target_len +/- tolerance where
    # target_len = plateau_before_up + plateau_middle_target +
    # plateau_after_down_start. One of the two has to be available, or
    # normalization has no layout at all.
    plateau_middle_target:
    plateau_length_tolerance:
  # Accepted for older configs. These keys do not remove rows.
  # Study group, sensor, and breath selection happens in the features stage.
  filters:
    use_feature_groups: false
    use_feature_sensor_types: false
    use_feature_breath_numbers: false
    include_study_groups: []
    include_sensor_types: []
    include_breath_numbers: []
    # Empty keeps every PCB. A non-empty list is applied at load, before
    # cut/align, and drops every other pcb_id. Quote each id: unquoted
    # values that look numeric lose their leading zeros.
    include_pcbs: []
  # Persistence keeps all columns.
  persistence:
    save_processed: true
    save_tracker: true
    save_section_landmarks: true
    # Explicit site-period and blocked-unit exclusions are audited but omitted
    # from processed.pkl by default.
    retain_excluded_override_rows: false
    # Preserve ordinary invalid SENSOR traces for invalid clustering/diagnostics.
    retain_invalid_sensor_rows: true
    # Preserve AUX/INDEX channels used by unit and temperature reports.
    retain_aux_index_rows: true

  aggregation_method: weighted_mean

- **Goal of W1:** no change to model numbers.

## Scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| L9 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Regression test only; fix was already on master (aac57b7) |
| L12 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | `apply_sensor_fusion` defaults to `none` instead of the removed `late` |
| L5 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Warning + reason when no threshold meets the sens/spec floors |
| L6 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Same warning, flag and reason on the two early-return paths |

| L4 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Aggregate result names its model (`aggregate_model_id`), adds `results_by_model()`, warns with >1 model |
| L1 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Wrong "reproduce exactly" comment corrected; draws unchanged |
| L2 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | `rotating` records `effective_fraction` and warns when slices ≠ proportion |
| L16 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Partition audit says what it checked (`scope`, `scope_note`) |
| L19 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | GRID_CLEAN doc uses Pipeline V2 keys and real paths |
| G2 | WONTFIX | WONTFIX | Password check recorded; notebook unchanged (see Decisions 4) |

11 findings: 10 FIXED, 1 recorded. No INVALID, NOT REPRODUCED or WAITING.

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 6312173 | L9 | Add a regression test for missing trigger landmarks |
| 83a310d | L12 | Default sensor fusion to the only mode that exists |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/train.py`**: `ThresholdClassifier.fit` (L5, L6). On the main training path, but the thresholds are the same; only a warning, the flag and a reason are added. The per-model table gets one new column, `threshold_fallback_reason`. Also a comment fix (L1).

**Tests:** 419 passed (baseline 386). The 33 extra are exactly the new W1 tests, and each one failed before its fix except the few that only pin existing behaviour. The failures, collection errors and SW-568 xfails are the same as the baseline, and the synthetic end-to-end system runs pass apart from the one baseline failure.

| Finding | What changed |
|---|---|
| L9 | Regression test only. On the pre-fix code it fails with the exact L9 crash. |
| L12 | Sensor fusion defaults to `none` instead of the removed `late`. |
| L5, L6 | All three silent fallbacks to a 0.5 threshold now warn and record why. |
| L3 | The training seed also covers NumPy's random generator. |
| L4 | The training result now says which model its summary fields describe, and warns when more than one model was trained. |
| L1, L2 | A wrong "reproduces old runs exactly" comment is corrected, and `rotating` warns when its slices can't match the requested proportion. |
| L16 | The partition audit now says what it actually checked. |
| L19 | The GRID_CLEAN doc uses the current config keys and real file paths. |

**Things to know before approving:**
- **G2 password:** the current `password=` in the notebook is a harmless placeholder that the database proxy replaces, so I left it. The real exposure is an **older 4-character `DB_PASSWORD` still readable in git history** (e.g. commit `0227e0f`). That's the question for Avichai: was it the real `postgres` password, and has it been rotated?
- **New issue for W8:** with several models and `source: training`, the model reports cover only the last model. I added it to W8 in the plan.
- **Tuning code is broken on master:** the tuning modules fail to import because of a field-order mistake in `FeatureTuningInput` (`src/core/balanced_rf_tuning.py`), introduced in `1bfe9ba`. Until it's fixed, the W7 tuning items (H6, M12, M13, L15) can't be tested.

**Questions for you** (also in the review note):
1. Should I fix the tuning import bug myself as a small separate commit before W2? It's a one-line change. Or should I open a ticket for Gilad?
2. For L1, is correcting the comment enough? Fixing the rounding itself would change some validation draws, so it would belong in W6/W7.

Review note: `C:\Users\82104\OneDrive\Documents\10. NANOSE\lucia\.claude.local\reviews\review_SW-589_W1.md`. It lists the commands to review the commits; the quickest is `git log --oneline sw589-W1-start..sw589-W1-review`, and the riskiest changes are in `src/core/train.py` and `src/core/stages/training.py`.

Waiting for your approval. I won't start W2 or push anything until you say "W1 approved".

@Avichai Toubi After investigating, I've proposed my solution and ideas of the implementations for 3 main groups:

  1. Cloud Team
    Members: Avichai, Tony, Gilad, Ilay

  • Project Owner role on the GCP project.
    This gives the team full control of project resources, deployments, infrastructure and services.

  • Organization Administrator role for Avichai, Gilad and Ilay only.
    This allows your team to manage organization-level IAM policies.

  • IAM Security Administrator may also be assigned to the same three users if they need to manage IAM policies across all Google Cloud resource types.

  1. Algo Team
    Additional restricted access for Eran and Lenny. Cloud Team members already have broader Owner access.

  • Cloud SQL Client role, restricted to the Clinical SQL instance.
    In addition, a database-level clinical_readonly role will be granted, allowing SELECT access to the Clinical database only. No insert, update, delete or schema changes will be allowed.

  • Storage Object User role on nanose_clinical_data and nanose_ml only.
    This allows file read/write operations in these two buckets, without access to other buckets or bucket configuration.

  • A custom VM Operator role on approved existing VMs only.
    This allows viewing, starting and stopping VMs. It does not allow creating, deleting, resizing or changing VM configuration.

  • A custom Cloud Run Job Operator role on approved Cloud Run Jobs only.
    This allows viewing Jobs, updating Job variables and running Jobs. It does not allow creating new Jobs or changing IAM policies.

  1. Dashboard Team
    Additional restricted access for Orit, Osnat and Omer Meroz.

  • Cloud Run Invoker role, or the equivalent IAP access role, on the Clinical Dashboard and Model Dashboard services only.
    This allows users to open the dashboards but does not provide direct access to Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, VMs, Cloud Run Jobs or service accounts.

@Avichai Toubi There are some insights from my investigation about the Service Account usage:

  • The default Compute service account is currently shared by 9 VMs, 2 dashboard services, and most Cloud Run Jobs. It has broad permissions, including Compute, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, Storage, and Secret Manager access. Its permissions should not be removed directly, as this could impact multiple current operation workloads. The recommended approach is to migrate workloads to dedicated service accounts first, then reduce the default account’s permissions.

  • The bitbucket-pipeline service account is actively used by CI/CD and several Cloud Run Jobs. It currently has broad administrative permissions, including Project IAM Admin, Cloud Run Admin, and Storage Admin. This should be separated into a limited CI/CD deployer account and dedicated runtime service accounts before permissions are reduced.

  • The experiment-status-api, application-uploader-sa, ecrf-eventarc-invoker, and ecrf-sync-workflow service accounts are linked to active services, external uploads, Eventarc triggers, or Workflows. No permissions were removed from these accounts.

  • The temporary temp-383 service account had no active workload, IAM permissions, user-managed key, or recent activity. It has been disabled and can be restored if needed.

  • The get-status-ml-api service account is inactive and has no identified workload, key, or explicit impersonation path. It only retains Cloud SQL access roles. It is a strong candidate for revoking these roles and disabling the account.

  • The write-ml-api service account is inactive. Its remaining Eventarc trigger points to a Cloud Run service that no longer exists. A decision is required to either retire this legacy flow and clean up the account, or restore the missing destination service.

  • The gilad-storage-access service account has no identified active project usage but still has an older user-managed key. Confirmation from Gilad is required before disabling or rotating the key.

@Avichai Toubi I believe after you grant Cloud SQL client permission into SA of VM, others VM can have access to Cloud SQL DB now.

However, this role only controls connectivity to the Cloud SQL instance. It does not control which PostgreSQL database or tables can be accessed.

Currently, the notebooks connect through the proxy using the shared built-in PostgreSQL user postgres and its password. Since this user has broad database privileges, any VM that has access to these credentials can access both the Clinical and Lab/AI databases. Therefore, granting Cloud SQL Client alone does not provide the required separation between VM access scopes.

There are two possible approaches:

  1. Keep built-in database authentication

    Create dedicated PostgreSQL users for each access scope, for example:

    • Clinical read-only user for standard VMs

    • Lab/AI user for you & Gilad development VMs

    Each user would receive only the required database permissions, and its password would be stored in Secret Manager. The notebooks would continue using Cloud SQL Proxy, but would no longer use the shared postgres account.

  2. Use IAM database authentication — recommended

    Assign a dedicated service account to each VM, or at least to each VM access tier. Configure Cloud SQL Proxy to use IAM database authentication, so the service account itself becomes the database identity.

    • Standard VM service accounts: read-only access to Clinical

    • Avichai and Gilad VM service accounts: access to Clinical plus Lab/AI databases

    • Other VM service accounts: no Lab/AI database access

    This removes the shared postgres password, enforces access based on the VM identity, and provides clearer audit logs showing which VM/service account accessed the database.

Please give your opinion about both solutions and decide which solution would be the best. I prefer the option 1 for now.
