tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

inputs.summary: SW-589 follow-up: G2 - remove the postgres admin user (IAM-only DB access)
inputs.description:
**Source:** SW-589, finding G2 in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` (lucia repo).

**Problem**
- The clinical data notebooks now connect with Cloud SQL IAM authentication (SW-553). The current `password=` in `notebooks/avichai/algo_data_download.ipynb` is only a placeholder that the proxy replaces with an IAM token.
- But an older hard-coded password for the built-in `postgres` user is still in the git history of `notebooks/General/algo_data_download.ipynb` (for example commit `0227e0f`). Anyone with read access to the repo can see it.
- SW-545 listed "update postgres user password" as remaining work, but it was closed without that step. Avichai confirmed on 2026-11-19 that the password is still valid.
- To use it, someone would also need Cloud SQL access through the proxy, but it bypasses the per-team IAM scopes (the `postgres` user can read Clinical and Lab/AI).

**Plan (from Avichai):** remove the admin user so the database accepts IAM logins only.

**Definition of done**
1. Confirm nothing still logs in as `postgres` with a password (Cloud Run jobs, dashboards, ETL, VMs, Secret Manager entries such as `etl-jobs-config`).
2. Rotate the `postgres` password to a new value that is not stored in any repo, or disable password login for it, so the value in git history no longer works.
3. Remove the admin user, or restrict it, so database access is IAM-only.
4. Comment here when done, so G2 in SW-589 can be closed.

The password value is deliberately not copied into this ticket.

inputs.description:
**Source:** SW-589, finding G2 in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` (lucia repo).

**Problem**
- The clinical data notebooks now connect with Cloud SQL IAM authentication (SW-553). The current `password=` in `notebooks/avichai/algo_data_download.ipynb` is only a placeholder that the proxy replaces with an IAM token.
- But an older hard-coded password for the built-in `postgres` user is still in the git history of `notebooks/General/algo_data_download.ipynb` (for example commit `0227e0f`). Anyone with read access to the repo can see it.
- SW-545 listed "update postgres user password" as remaining work, but it was closed without that step. Avichai confirmed on 2026-11-19 that the password is still valid.
- To use it, someone would also need Cloud SQL access through the proxy, but it bypasses the per-team IAM scopes (the `postgres` user can read Clinical and Lab/AI).

**Plan (from Avichai):** remove the admin user so the database accepts IAM logins only.

**Definition of done**
1. Confirm nothing still logs in as `postgres` with a password (Cloud Run jobs, dashboards, ETL, VMs, Secret Manager entries such as `etl-jobs-config`).
2. Rotate the `postgres` password to a new value that is not stored in any repo, or disable password login for it, so the value in git history no longer works.
3. Remove the admin user, or restrict it, so database access is IAM-only.
4. Comment here when done, so G2 in SW-589 can be closed.

The password value is deliberately not copied into this ticket.

content.text:
Question 2 isn't about any finding in the file. It's a bug I found while recording the W1 baseline: **the tuning modules can't be imported on master.**

- **Where:** `FeatureTuningInput` in `src/core/balanced_rf_tuning.py`. `positive_labels` has a default value but comes before `feature_run_id`, which doesn't, and Python rejects that order in a dataclass. It came in with commit `1bfe9ba` (Gilad, 2026-11-09), the same commit that fixed M1/H6.
- **Effect:** `balanced_rf_tuning`, `xgboost_tuning` and `easy_ensemble_tuning` all fail on import. Three of the 4 collection errors in the baseline come from this.

**Which findings it blocks.** These are all W7 items that need the tuning code to run their tests:

| Finding | Why it needs tuning |
|---|---|
| **H6** | Its fix is already on master, but its regression test compares tuning's threshold folds with production's. That needs `balanced_rf_tuning` to import. |
| **M12** | Tuning searches the sensitivity/specificity floors. Lives in the tuning configs and code. |
| **M13** | Best trial picked from a single CV split. In `balanced_rf_tuning.py:438, 584`. |
| **L15** | Tuning reproducibility and xgboost version pins. |
| **Q4** | Should production threshold folds match tuning's? Linked to H6. |

M1's test doesn't need it, because `ThresholdClassifier` is in `train.py`.

That's why I asked: since it isn't one of the 69 findings, the plan doesn't cover it. Your options are:
- **Fix it myself:** a one-line field move, as its own commit before W7.
- **Open a ticket for Gilad:** it came in with his commit.

Either way, it has to be fixed before W7 can be tested.

message.content: elaborate on item L1 for me. What is the issue here?

content.text:
L1 is about how many patients go into the validation set on each permutation, and whether the new code picks the same number as the old code.

### Background
On every permutation, training holds out `val_size`% of each study group's patients (e.g. 20% of the LC patients and 20% of the NOT_LC patients) as validation, then trains on the rest. The number to hold out is `pool size × val_size / 100`, rounded.

- **Old code** (`_select_validation_patients_by_percent`, from before Pipeline V2): `round(n * val_size / 100)`, capped at `n − 1`.
- **New code** (`_n_to_draw` in `partition_testing.py`): `round(n * (val_size / 100))`, capped at `n`.

A comment in `train.py` said the new code makes "existing runs reproduce exactly". The finding says that's not always true.

### Difference 1: rounding order
Computers store most decimals slightly off, so the order of the arithmetic can change the result:

| | Calculation | Result | Rounded |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old | 90 × 35 / 100 | exactly 31.5 | **32** |
| New | 90 × 0.35 | 31.499999999999996 | **31** |

So with `val_size: 35` and a group of 90 patients, the new code validates **one patient fewer**. Up to pools of 400 this happens for 11 percentages (7, 14, 34, 35, 41, 55, 57, 58, 69, 70, 82). It never happens for 20% or 11.1111%, the two values the shipped configs use. My test checks those two up to pools of 1,999.

The effect is bigger than one patient. Training draws validation patients from Python's shared random number stream. A different count uses up a different amount of that stream, so **that permutation and every permutation after it** get different validation sets, which means different metrics.

### Difference 2: the cap
The old code never put more than `n − 1` patients into validation, so each group always kept at least one training patient. The new code caps at `n`, so a group with a single patient puts that patient into validation, and **that group has no training patient** in that permutation. That's more than a reproducibility detail. It only happens with tiny groups, though; the old code put such a patient into training every time.

### Who is affected today
Nobody, with the shipped configs. 20% and 11.1111% match the old code for any group of 2 or more patients. It matters if someone:
- uses a different percentage (e.g. 35%) and compares against old notebook runs. The numbers won't match and nothing explains why, because the comment says they should; or
- runs a group (or site subset) with only one patient.

### What W1 did, and the choice left
W1 made the comment true and added a test that pins down both differences. No draws changed, which keeps W1's "no number changes" rule.

The open choice (question 3):
- **Keep it as is:** documented, and current runs unaffected.
- **Match the old code:** round as `n * val_size / 100` and cap at `n − 1`. That restores exact reproduction of old runs and stops a group losing its only training patient. It does change validation draws for the affected percentages and tiny groups, so it would go in W6/W7 with a before/after comparison.

I'd recommend at least the cap (`n − 1`) as a later fix, because losing the only training patient is a real defect, not just a mismatch with old runs.

I created it. It didn't exist on master (`de32631`), and git shows it was added in commit `738af71` "SW-589 L5, L6: Warn when the threshold falls back to 0.5".

It's the test for L5 and L6. It covers the three ways `ThresholdClassifier.fit` used to fall back to the 0.5 threshold without saying so, plus one normal case:

| Test | Situation | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `test_constraints_nobody_can_meet_warn_and_flag_the_fallback` | L5: no threshold meets `min_sensitivity`/`min_specificity` | warning raised, `threshold_ == 0.5`, `threshold_fallback_reason_ == "constraints_unmet"` |

| `test_too_few_patients_per_class_warns_and_flags_the_fallback` | L6: a class has fewer than 2 patients, so no cross-validation | warning, flag `True`, reason `"too_few_patients"` |
| `test_normal_fit_does_not_warn_and_is_not_a_fallback` | normal fit | no warning, flag `False`, reason `None` |

I wrote it before changing the code. All four tests failed on master's `train.py`, then passed after the fix. The data is small and synthetic, generated in the test itself, so no clinical files are used.

Yes, I'd do it. One change: make them **sub-tasks of SW-589**, not separate tasks with "relates to" links. The SW project has a `Subtask` type.

**Why per-workstream tickets help:**
- **Due date:** SW-589 is due 2026-11-24, and most of the work (W2–W9) won't be done by then. With one ticket per workstream, Avichai and Gilad can see what's finished and what's still to come, instead of one ticket that stays "In Progress" for weeks.
- **They match how you already work.** Each workstream already has an approval checkpoint and a review note. The ticket status can follow that cycle: To Do → In Progress → In Review (when the review note is written) → Done (when you approve and it merges).
- **Reviewers know what to look at.** Gilad and Avichai can see which findings each workstream closes and which ones change model numbers (W4, W5, W7), so they can focus their review there.
- **Follow-ups have a home.** Tickets like SW-593 can link to the workstream they came from.

**Why sub-tasks rather than linked tasks:**
- They show up directly on SW-589's page with their status, so Avichai sees progress without clicking through links.
- SW-589 can then be closed once all its sub-tasks are done, or once the rest have been moved to follow-up tickets.
- "Relates to" links are better for something separate, like SW-593.

**What I'd create:** 10 sub-tasks, W0–W9, all assigned to you. Each would have:
- **Title:** `SW-589 W<n>: <workstream name>`, e.g. `SW-589 W2: Run provenance and tracker`.
- **Description:** the findings it covers, whether it changes model numbers, which PR it belongs to (PR 1–5 from the plan), and dependencies (e.g. W7 needs the tuning fix, which is done).
- **W0 and W1:** created and set to **Done**, with a short comment summarising the results (10 findings fixed, 427 tests passing, SW-593 opened, tuning import fixed).
- **W2–W9:** To Do.

**Two things to consider first:**
1. **Mention it to Avichai at the daily meeting,** since the sub-tasks go under his ticket. It's normal practice, but he may prefer one ticket per PR (5 instead of 10). That would match the review cycle Gilad and Avichai will see.
2. **Jira has no "In Review" status in this project** as far as I've seen. I can check the available statuses before creating anything, so the workflow matches what's really there.

Should I create the 10 sub-tasks now, or wait until you've checked with Avichai?

content.text:
I added **33 test cases** in W1. They come from 24 test functions, because some functions run once per input (for example, once per sensor-fusion mode). Here's the count per finding, taken from pytest's collected list:

| Finding | Test cases | Test file | What they cover |
|---|---|---|---|
| L9 | 4 | `test_trigger_detection_anchors.py` | NaN up trigger, NaN down trigger, missing up tuple, missing down tuple |
| L12 | 6 | `test_sensor_fusion.py` | default is a valid mode (1); default call returns data unchanged (1); each removed mode still raises when asked for (4) |
| L5 | 1 | `test_threshold_fallback.py` | no threshold meets the sens/spec floors |
| L6 | 2 | `test_threshold_fallback.py` | single-class training set; fewer than 2 patients in a class |
| L5 + L6 | 1 | `test_threshold_fallback.py` | a normal fit doesn't warn or flag a fallback (shared check) |
| L3 | 2 | `test_training_seed.py` | same seed gives same draws; outer random state restored |
| L4 | 2 | `test_training_stage.py` | several models: names the model and warns; one model: no warning |
| L1 | 3 | `test_partition_sizes.py` | matches the old count for 20% and 11.1111% (2); the documented differences are real (1) |
| L2 | 2 | `test_partition_sizes.py` | 30% warns (3 slices of 33%); 20% stays silent |
| L16 | 4 | `test_partition_audit_scope.py` | default scope; recorded-run scope; note shown in the report; `test_partitions` audits its own plan |
| L19 | 6 | `test_grid_clean_doc.py` | every path exists; every function exists; every config key exists; no `process.` / `filter.` / `load.` keys (3) |
| G2 | 0 | — | checked and recorded only, no code change |
| **Total** | **33** | | |

If you want this in sub-task 1, I'd keep it to one line to match the short style, e.g. "**Tests:** 33 new test cases (at least one per fixed finding); each failed before its change and passes after. Full suite: 427 passed, no new failures." The per-finding breakdown would stay in this conversation and the W1 review note.

One correction to that line: not every one of the 33 failed before its change. The ones that check behaviour that was already correct passed both times:
- L1: all 3 (the fix was only to a comment).
- L12: the 4 "removed modes still raise" cases.
- L9: all 4 ran against master, where the fix already existed. I proved them on the pre-fix commit instead, where the two NaN cases crash and the two tuple cases fail.

So the accurate wording would be: "each fix has at least one test that failed before the change". Should I use that?

from src.datasets import cache_dataset_from_config, sha256_file

STAGE_ORDER = (
    "preprocessing",
    "clustering",
    "features",
    "holdout",
    "training",
    "visualization",
    "model_reports",
)
STAGE_DEPENDENCIES = {
    "preprocessing": (),
    "clustering": ("preprocessing",),
    "features": ("clustering",),
    "holdout": ("features",),
    "training": ("features",),
    "visualization": ("clustering",),
    # Or ("holdout",) when model_reports reads a holdout run; see _dependencies.
    "model_reports": ("training",),
}
REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS = {
    "preprocessing": (
        "processed.pkl",
        "tracker.pkl",
        "section_landmarks.json",
    ),
    "clustering": ("clustered.pkl", "clustered_invalid.pkl"),
    "features": (
        "features/train_validation_set.pkl",
        "features/test_set.pkl",
        "features/estimation_pickle.pkl",
        "features/feature_selector.json",
    ),
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunnerOptions:
    config_path: Path | None = None
    run_dir: Path | None = None
    clinical_paths: Sequence[Path] | None = None
    cli_overrides: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
    from_stage: str | None = None
    to_stage: str | None = None
    stages: frozenset[str] | None = None
    resume: bool = False
    force: bool = False
    dry_run: bool = False
    repo_root: Path | None = None
    now: datetime | None = None
    # Processes the holdout stage trains its holdouts on.
    holdout_jobs: int = 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StageExecutionResult:
    stage: str
    status: str
    result: Any | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PipelineExecutionResult:
    config: ResolvedPipelineConfig
    run: PipelineRun | None
    planned_stages: tuple[str, ...]
    stages: tuple[StageExecutionResult, ...]


def _validate_stage(stage: str | None, field_name: str) -> None:

"""Holdout training stage: per-holdout feature selection + Monte-Carlo training.

The algorithm is the one of ``notebooks/gilad/pipeline_v2_holdout_training*.ipynb``:

1. Rows of a completed feature run's ``features_all.pkl`` are filtered to the
   configured sites, labels and ``aggregated_reason == VALID``.
2. Test-only patients are taken out first. They are never trained on and join
   the test set of every holdout; their site decides whether they are
   ``in_cohort`` (a training site) or ``other_sites``.
3. The remaining selection pool is split into holdout test groups (``mode``):
   ``kfold`` (stratified, every pool patient tested once), ``random`` (a random
   ``test_percent`` of each class per holdout), ``sites`` (one holdout testing
   ``test_sites``), ``fold_plan`` (a pinned plan, e.g. the TYPE1-61 person-level
   folds) or ``test_only`` (the test set is the test-only patients alone).
4. Per holdout, features are selected on train_validation only, then every
   selected model is trained ``training.permutations`` times with a fresh
   validation draw and scored on the constant holdout test set.

Outputs live under ``<run>/holdout_runs/[<run_group>/]<stamp>_holdout_train_run_<label>/``
with one ``holdout_XX/`` folder per holdout and the pooled run-level tables.

content.content:
# Holdout training

The `holdout` stage trains and evaluates models over several patient-disjoint
holdouts of one feature run. Per holdout it selects features on the
train/validation patients only, then trains every selected model for
`training.permutations` Monte-Carlo validation draws against a constant test
set. Afterwards it pools every patient's test predictions over the holdouts.

## Running it

```bash
# preprocessing -> clustering -> features -> holdout
python scripts/lucia_pipeline.py holdout --config path/to/run.yaml

# holdouts only, on a run whose features stage is complete
python scripts/lucia_pipeline.py holdout --run-dir ~/lucia-runs/<run_id> --config path/to/run.yaml

# check the plan without running anything
python scripts/lucia_pipeline.py holdout --dry-run --config path/to/run.yaml
```

`--set holdout.max_holdouts=1` runs only the first holdout (a smoke run).
`publish-results` uploads `holdout_runs/` with the rest of the run.

With `--run-dir`, `--config` is an overlay on the run's frozen
`resolved_config.yaml`: only its `holdout`, `training`, `model_reports` and
`features.{n_features,selection_method,selection_kwargs}` are applied, so
preprocessing, clustering and extraction stay as the run froze them. `--set`
is applied after the overlay. Overlays and `--set` both merge mappings into the
run's (and `--set` skips `null`), so keys of a mapping such as
`selection_kwargs` can be added or changed but never removed.

`notebooks/gilad/pipeline_v2_holdout_training.ipynb` does the same from a
notebook (`RUN_DIR`, `OVERLAY_CONFIG`, `CLI_OVERRIDES`), and
`src.core.stages.preview_holdout(run, config)` returns the cohort, plan and
assignment table without training or writing anything.

The `holdout:` section of `configs/pipeline/validation_only.yaml` documents
every key. Models, `permutations`, `val_size` and `validation_partition_plan`
come from `training:`; `n_features`, `selection_method` and `selection_kwargs`

def _dropped_files_summary(
        self,
        *,
        known_files: pd.Series | None,
        study_group_col: str,
        set_col: str,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """One row per (study_group, 'dropped') for files absent from
        ``known_files`` but present in the initial-load snapshot -- i.e.
        removed entirely before reaching feature extraction."""
        initial = self._initial_files_df
        if initial is None or initial.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame()
        known = set(known_files.dropna().unique()) if known_files is not None else set()
        dropped = initial.loc[~initial["file_write_time"].isin(known)]
        if dropped.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame()
        dropped = dropped.rename(columns={"ecrf_study_group": study_group_col})
        dropped = dropped.assign(**{set_col: DROPPED_SET_LABEL})
        return (
            dropped.groupby([study_group_col, set_col], dropna=False, as_index=False)
            .agg(
                n_file_write_times=("file_write_time", "nunique"),
                n_patients=("patient_id", "nunique"),
                n_rows=("file_write_time", "size"),
            )
        )

# Zero/negative spans are invalid DB sentinel geometry (for example
    # up_trig=down_trig=0 with [-1, 0] tuples), not real plateau lengths.
    # Letting a large invalid cohort contribute zeros can collapse the derived
    # layout even when trigger detection recovered valid landmarks elsewhere.
    valid_middle = work["_middle_len"].notna() & work["_middle_len"].gt(0)
    mid_all = work.loc[valid_middle, "_middle_len"]
    if mid_all.empty:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"grid_clean median filter: not one of {len(work)} traces has a readable middle "
            f"length greater than zero. Both {up_col!r} and {down_col!r} are present; "
            "check whether the DB landmarks are unresolved sentinels and whether "
            "trigger detection recovered them."
        )

    global_median_mid = float(mid_all.median())
    mask = valid_middle & (
        (work["_middle_len"] >= global_median_mid - tol_below)
        & (work["_middle_len"] <= global_median_mid + tol_above)
    )
    filtered = work[mask].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
    print(
        f"[preprocess/grid_clean] cohort middle length (up start -> down start): "
        f"median={global_median_mid:.1f} from {len(mid_all)} traces, "
        f"keep [{global_median_mid - tol_below:.0f},{global_median_mid + tol_above:.0f}] "
        f"(median -{tol_below} / +{tol_above}): {len(filtered)}/{len(work)} rows"
    )

    middle_target = int(round(global_median_mid))
    cfg_out = {
        **cfg,
        "plateau_middle_target": middle_target,
        "plateau_length_tolerance": None,
        "median_from_up_start_to_down_start": median_from_up_start,
    }
    if median_from_up_start:
        cfg_out["plateau_min_len"] = before_up + int(global_median_mid - tol_below) + after_down_start
        cfg_out["plateau_max_len"] = before_up + int(global_median_mid + tol_above) + after_down_start
        print(
            f"[preprocess/grid_clean] derived layout: {before_up} + {middle_target} + "
            f"{after_down_start} = {before_up + middle_target + after_down_start} samples, "
            f"accepted cut length [{cfg_out['plateau_min_len']},{cfg_out['plateau_max_len']}]"
        )
    return filtered.drop(columns=["_middle_len"], errors="ignore"), cfg_out

    tolerance = cfg.get("plateau_length_tolerance")

    # down_section_tuple_new = (down_start, down_start + down_feature_length) — only the descent feature, not seg5.

    else:

    up_final = []
    down_final = []
    for up_n, down_n in zip(up_new_list, down_new_list):
        u0, u1 = up_n[0], up_n[1]
        d0, d1 = down_n[0], down_n[1]
        u_end = min(u0 + up_feature_length, target_len)
        if down_start_fixed is not None:

        d_end = min(d0 + down_feature_length, target_len)
        up_final.append((u0, u_end))
        down_final.append((d0, d_end))
    df["up_section_tuple_new"] = up_final
    df["down_section_tuple_new"] = down_final

    df["RAW_signal_cut"] = df["RAW_SIGNAL_CUT"]
    if logger:
        msg = (
            f"Plateau normalization: {len(df)} signals to length {target_len} "
            f"(plateau_before_up={before_up}, plateau_after_down_start={after_down_start}"
            + (f", plateau_middle_target={plateau_middle_target}" if plateau_middle_target is not None else "")
            + f", up_feature_length={up_feature_length}, down_feature_length={down_feature_length})"
        )
        if smooth_all:
            msg += f", smooth_all (window={savgol_window}, poly={savgol_poly})"
        elif smooth_all_except:
            msg += f", smooth_all_except (seg1+seg3+tail of seg4, window={savgol_window}, poly={savgol_poly}) [applied to {n_savgol_applied}/{len(df)} signals]"
        elif savgol_before_resize:
            msg += f", smooth_mid on seg3 only (window={savgol_window}, poly={savgol_poly}) [applied to {n_savgol_applied}/{len(df)} signals]"
        msg += f", plateau_alignment={plateau_alignment_method}"

def run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cut, align, and z-score signals using the shared plateau normalizer."""

    grid_clean_df = prepare_grid_clean_plateau_df(df)
    grid_clean_df = apply_grid_clean_trigger_detection(grid_clean_df)
    n_before_median = len(grid_clean_df)
    if cfg.get("use_breath_median_for_alignment") and cfg.get("plateau_median_global"):
        grid_clean_df, cfg = apply_grid_clean_median_filter(grid_clean_df, cfg)

    if cfg.get("plateau_middle_target") is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "GRID_CLEAN preprocess has no plateau layout: the median gate is off "
            "(use_breath_median_for_alignment / plateau_median_global) and "
            "plateau_middle_target was not set. Either leave the gate on so the "
            "layout is measured from the cohort, or configure plateau_middle_target "
            "with plateau_min_len / plateau_max_len explicitly. Without one of the "
            "two, apply_plateau_normalization silently falls back to its generic "
            "signal_length layout, which is not the GRID_CLEAN geometry."
        )

    print(
        "[preprocess/grid_clean] plateau norm: "
        f"before_up={cfg['plateau_before_up']}, after_down={cfg['plateau_after_down_start']}, "
        f"up_feat={cfg['up_feature_length']}, down_feat={cfg['down_feature_length']}, "
        f"window start offsets up/down="
        f"{cfg.get('up_feature_start_offset')}/{cfg.get('down_feature_start_offset')} (applied), "
        f"align={cfg['plateau_alignment_method']}, "
        f"smooth_all_except={cfg.get('smooth_all_except')}"
    )
    # apply_plateau_normalization anchors its cut on `up_section_tuple` /
    # `down_section_tuple` by those names, and a frame that carries the landmarks under
    # the other pair -- which is how they arrive before the schema mapper renames them
    # -- makes it fall back to a generic resample of the whole cut. That fallback is not
    # this geometry: the rise no longer lands on `plateau_before_up`, so the feature
    # windows stop pointing at the transitions. It is also silent, since the warning
    # goes to a logger. So the names are supplied here, and the result is checked below.
    up_col, down_col = section_tuple_columns(grid_clean_df)
    for resolved, required in ((up_col, "up_section_tuple"),
                               (down_col, "down_section_tuple")):
        if required not in grid_clean_df.columns:
            grid_clean_df[required] = grid_clean_df[resolved]

    # Keep the GRID_CLEAN-facing config descriptive while adapting to the shared
    # plateau-normalization API. This string does not escape this boundary.
    normalization_cfg = {
        **cfg,
        "plateau_alignment_method": (
            "crop_pad" if cfg["plateau_alignment_method"] == "crop_pad" else "cubic"
        ),
    }
    normalized = apply_plateau_normalization(grid_clean_df, normalization_cfg, logger=None)
    if "up_section_tuple_new" not in normalized.columns:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "the plateau alignment fell back to a generic resample: its output carries "
            "no 'up_section_tuple_new'. The GRID_CLEAN geometry needs the plateau path, which "
            "needs 'RAWData' and the section tuples in the frame. Nothing downstream "
            "can tell the two apart, so this stops here rather than returning traces "
            "whose feature windows do not sit on the transitions."
        )
    out = finalize_grid_clean_plateau_df(normalized, cfg)
    out.attrs["grid_clean_derived_layout"] = {
        **derived_grid_clean_layout(cfg),
        "n_before_median": n_before_median,
        "n_after_median": len(grid_clean_df),
    }
    return out


def preprocess_dataframe_grid_clean(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    cfg: dict | None = None,
    geometry: dict | None = None,
    overrides: dict | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Public GRID_CLEAN GRID_CLEAN preprocess entry (replaces Gilad cut+align+L2)."""
    if cfg is None:
        resolved = effective_grid_clean_preprocess_cfg(overrides=overrides, geometry=geometry)
    else:

def run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cut, align, and z-score signals using the shared plateau normalizer."""

    grid_clean_df = prepare_grid_clean_plateau_df(df)
    grid_clean_df = apply_grid_clean_trigger_detection(grid_clean_df)
    n_before_median = len(grid_clean_df)
    if cfg.get("use_breath_median_for_alignment") and cfg.get("plateau_median_global"):
        grid_clean_df, cfg = apply_grid_clean_median_filter(grid_clean_df, cfg)

    if cfg.get("plateau_middle_target") is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "GRID_CLEAN preprocess has no plateau layout: the median gate is off "
            "(use_breath_median_for_alignment / plateau_median_global) and "
            "plateau_middle_target was not set. Either leave the gate on so the "
            "layout is measured from the cohort, or configure plateau_middle_target "
            "with plateau_min_len / plateau_max_len explicitly. Without one of the "
            "two, apply_plateau_normalization silently falls back to its generic "
            "signal_length layout, which is not the GRID_CLEAN geometry."
        )

    print(
        "[preprocess/grid_clean] plateau norm: "
        f"before_up={cfg['plateau_before_up']}, after_down={cfg['plateau_after_down_start']}, "
        f"up_feat={cfg['up_feature_length']}, down_feat={cfg['down_feature_length']}, "
        f"window start offsets up/down="
        f"{cfg.get('up_feature_start_offset')}/{cfg.get('down_feature_start_offset')} (applied), "
        f"align={cfg['plateau_alignment_method']}, "
        f"smooth_all_except={cfg.get('smooth_all_except')}"
    )
    # apply_plateau_normalization anchors its cut on `up_section_tuple` /
    # `down_section_tuple` by those names, and a frame that carries the landmarks under
    # the other pair -- which is how they arrive before the schema mapper renames them
    # -- makes it fall back to a generic resample of the whole cut. That fallback is not
    # this geometry: the rise no longer lands on `plateau_before_up`, so the feature
    # windows stop pointing at the transitions. It is also silent, since the warning
    # goes to a logger. So the names are supplied here, and the result is checked below.
    up_col, down_col = section_tuple_columns(grid_clean_df)
    for resolved, required in ((up_col, "up_section_tuple"),
                               (down_col, "down_section_tuple")):
        if required not in grid_clean_df.columns:
            grid_clean_df[required] = grid_clean_df[resolved]

    # Keep the GRID_CLEAN-facing config descriptive while adapting to the shared
    # plateau-normalization API. This string does not escape this boundary.
    normalization_cfg = {
        **cfg,
        "plateau_alignment_method": (
            "crop_pad" if cfg["plateau_alignment_method"] == "crop_pad" else "cubic"
        ),
    }
    normalized = apply_plateau_normalization(grid_clean_df, normalization_cfg, logger=None)
    if "up_section_tuple_new" not in normalized.columns:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "the plateau alignment fell back to a generic resample: its output carries "
            "no 'up_section_tuple_new'. The GRID_CLEAN geometry needs the plateau path, which "
            "needs 'RAWData' and the section tuples in the frame. Nothing downstream "
            "can tell the two apart, so this stops here rather than returning traces "
            "whose feature windows do not sit on the transitions."
        )
    out = finalize_grid_clean_plateau_df(normalized, cfg)
    out.attrs["grid_clean_derived_layout"] = {
        **derived_grid_clean_layout(cfg),
        "n_before_median": n_before_median,
        "n_after_median": len(grid_clean_df),
    }
    return out


def preprocess_dataframe_grid_clean(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    cfg: dict | None = None,
    geometry: dict | None = None,
    overrides: dict | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Public GRID_CLEAN GRID_CLEAN preprocess entry (replaces Gilad cut+align+L2)."""
    if cfg is None:
        resolved = effective_grid_clean_preprocess_cfg(overrides=overrides, geometry=geometry)
    else:
        merged = dict(cfg)
        if geometry:
            merged.update(geometry)
        if overrides:
            merged.update(overrides)
        resolved = effective_grid_clean_preprocess_cfg(overrides=merged)
    return run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(df, resolved)

def record_removed_traces(
        self,
        stage: str,
        reason: str,
        removed: pd.DataFrame | list[dict[str, Any]],
        *,
        trace_reason_col: str | None = None,
        detail_col: str | None = None,
        metadata_cols: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Append one entry per removed trace (file_write_time + device_channel).

        Each ``(file_write_time, device_channel)`` is kept only once (first wins).
        """
        if isinstance(removed, list):
            rows = removed
        else:
            if removed.empty:
                return
            rows = removed.to_dict(orient="records")

        metadata_cols = metadata_cols or []
        started_at = self._started_at_for(stage)
        for row in rows:
            if isinstance(row, pd.Series):
                row = row.to_dict()

            file_write_time = row.get("file_write_time")
            device_channel = row.get("device_channel")
            # Keyed by stage+reason (not just the trace) so a trace that becomes
            # invalid for one reason can still be recorded again if it later
            # becomes invalid for a *different* reason (e.g. marked
            # INVALID_overide_by_period, then re-marked INVALID_overide_by_unit_number).
            key = (file_write_time, device_channel, stage, reason)
            if key in self._removed_trace_keys:
                continue
            self._removed_trace_keys.add(key)

            if trace_reason_col and trace_reason_col in row:
                trace_reason = str(row[trace_reason_col])
            else:
                trace_reason = reason

            detail = ""
            if detail_col and detail_col in row and row[detail_col] is not None:
                detail = str(row[detail_col])

            meta = {col: row[col] for col in metadata_cols if col in row}
            self.removed_traces.append(
                RemovedTrace(
                    stage=stage,
                    reason=trace_reason,
                    file_write_time=file_write_time,
                    device_channel=device_channel,
                    detail=detail,
                    started_at=started_at,
                    event_reason=reason,
                    metadata=meta,
                )
            )

        self,
        stage: str,
        reason: str,
        df_before: pd.DataFrame,
        df_after: pd.DataFrame,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        trace_reason_col: str | None = None,
        detail_col: str | None = None,
        metadata_cols: list[str] | None = None,
        section: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Record summary counts and per-trace invalidations from a row filter.

        Rows removed outright (present in ``df_before``, absent from
        ``df_after``) are recorded as invalid traces, and so are rows that
        stayed but are invalid in ``df_after`` -- either because their
        ``aggregated_reason`` changed to a non-VALID value ("mark, don't
        drop" stages like ``override_by_site_period``), or because
        ``aggregated_reason`` didn't exist yet in ``df_before`` (the very
        first time it's computed, e.g. schema/load_pickle: every row that
        comes out non-VALID is "born invalid" there). Either way they count
        toward this stage/reason's invalid trace total, feeding
        ``invalid_traces``/``removed_by_file``.
        """
        self.record(
            stage,
        )
    _require_columns(
        out,
        [MODIFIED_SIGNAL_CUT_COL, UP_TUPLE_CUT_COL, DOWN_TUPLE_CUT_COL],
        "signal cut",
    )
    if tracker and failed:
        tracker.record(
            "signal_cut", "cut_failed", n_before, len(out), {"n_failed": len(failed)}, df_after=out
        )
        tracker.record_removed_traces(
            "signal_cut",
            "cut_failed",
            failed,
            detail_col="error",
        )

    out["sig_len"] = out[MODIFIED_SIGNAL_CUT_COL].apply(len)

    if signal_length_range:
        lo, hi = signal_length_range
        before_len = out
        out = filter_dataframe_rows(out, (out["sig_len"] >= lo) & (out["sig_len"] <= hi))
        if tracker:
            tracker.record_filter(
                "signal_cut",
                f"length_not_in_{lo}_{hi}",
                before_len,
                out,
                detail_col="sig_len",
                metadata_cols=["sig_len"],

    def _has_length(value: Any, expected: int) -> bool:
        return (
            isinstance(value, (list, tuple))
            and len(value) >= 2
            and int(value[1]) - int(value[0]) == expected
        )

    complete = out["up_section_tuple_new"].map(
        lambda value: _has_length(value, up_target)
    ) & out["down_section_tuple_new"].map(
        lambda value: _has_length(value, down_target)
    )
    if not bool(complete.all()):
        print(
            "[preprocess/grid_clean] dropping "
            f"{int((~complete).sum())} trace(s) too short for the configured "
            "UP/DOWN feature windows"
        )
        out = out.loc[complete].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
    if out.empty:
        raise ValueError(
            "GRID_CLEAN preprocessing left no traces with complete UP/DOWN "
            "feature windows"
        )
    if "normalized_resampled_signals" in out.columns:
        out["resampled_signals"] = out["normalized_resampled_signals"]
    audit_grid_clean_section_lengths(out, cfg)
    return out

"""SW-589 M11: GRID_CLEAN drops must reach the removal audit, not only stdout."""
import pandas as pd

import src.core.grid_clean_preprocess as gc
from src.core.removal_audit import Tracker


def _frame():
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "file_write_time": ["f1", "f2", "f3", "f4"],
            "device_channel": [1, 1, 1, 1],
            "patient_id": ["p1", "p2", "p3", "p4"],
            "aggregated_reason": ["VALID"] * 4,
        }
    )


def _drop(file_write_time):
    def step(df, *args, **kwargs):
        out = df.loc[df["file_write_time"] != file_write_time].reset_index(drop=True)
        return out

    return step


def _stub_steps(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "prepare_grid_clean_plateau_df", lambda df: df.copy())
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "apply_grid_clean_trigger_detection", lambda df: df)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        gc,
        "apply_grid_clean_median_filter",
        lambda df, cfg: (_drop("f1")(df), {**cfg, "plateau_middle_target": 100}),
    )

    def normalize(df, cfg, logger=None):
        out = _drop("f2")(df)
        out["up_section_tuple_new"] = [(0, 1)] * len(out)
        return out

    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "apply_plateau_normalization", normalize)
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "finalize_grid_clean_plateau_df", lambda df, cfg: _drop("f3")(df))
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "section_tuple_columns", lambda df: ("up_section_tuple", "down_section_tuple"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "derived_grid_clean_layout", lambda cfg: {})


def _cfg():
    return {
        "use_breath_median_for_alignment": True,
        "plateau_median_global": True,
        "plateau_before_up": 30,
        "plateau_after_down_start": 90,
        "up_feature_length": 45,
        "down_feature_length": 60,
        "plateau_alignment_method": "crop_pad",
    }


def test_each_grid_clean_drop_is_recorded_with_its_reason(monkeypatch):
    _stub_steps(monkeypatch)
    tracker = Tracker()
    frame = _frame().assign(up_section_tuple=[(0, 1)] * 4, down_section_tuple=[(2, 3)] * 4)

    out = gc.run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(frame, _cfg(), tracker=tracker)

    assert out["file_write_time"].tolist() == ["f4"]
    removed = tracker.removed_traces_df()
    by_reason = removed.set_index("event_reason")["file_write_time"].to_dict()
    assert by_reason == {
        "grid_clean_median_gate": "f1",
        "grid_clean_length_filter": "f2",
        "grid_clean_incomplete_feature_window": "f3",
    }
    events = tracker.to_dataframe().set_index("reason")
    assert events.loc["grid_clean_median_gate", "n_removed"] == 1
    assert events.loc["grid_clean_length_filter", "n_remaining"] == 2
    assert events.loc["grid_clean_incomplete_feature_window", "n_remaining"] == 1
    assert set(events["stage"]) == {"grid_clean"}


def test_no_event_when_a_step_drops_nothing(monkeypatch):
    _stub_steps(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(gc, "finalize_grid_clean_plateau_df", lambda df, cfg: df)
    tracker = Tracker()
    frame = _frame().assign(up_section_tuple=[(0, 1)] * 4, down_section_tuple=[(2, 3)] * 4)

    gc.run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(frame, _cfg(), tracker=tracker)

    assert "grid_clean_incomplete_feature_window" not in set(tracker.to_dataframe()["reason"])


def test_without_a_tracker_nothing_changes(monkeypatch):
    _stub_steps(monkeypatch)
    frame = _frame().assign(up_section_tuple=[(0, 1)] * 4, down_section_tuple=[(2, 3)] * 4)

    out = gc.run_grid_clean_plateau_normalization(frame, _cfg())

    assert out["file_write_time"].tolist() == ["f4"]

# Review: SW-589 W2, run provenance and tracker

- **Status:** `[r]` awaiting Tram's review · **Jira:** SW-595 (In Progress)
- **Branch:** `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings`
- **Range:** `sw589-W2-start..sw589-W2-review` (4 commits)
- **Goal of W2:** every run records the code that produced it and every row it removed. No change to model numbers.

## Scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| G5 | FIXED (0df6cd8) | FIXED, **now with tests** | 2 regression tests: no base `features/` folder for new runs; old runs still load |
| G13 | FIXED (0df6cd8) | FIXED, **tests confirmed** | Tests already came with the fix; checked that they catch the defect. Docs only |
| G12 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Audit counts remaining visits (`n_remaining_visits`, `n_visits` per set) |
| M11 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | GRID_CLEAN drops recorded in the audit with their reason |
| G18 | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED, **question for Gilad** | Not changed; the intent is unclear (Question 1) |
| L13 | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED, **question for Gilad/Avichai** | Not changed; it's a default decision (Question 2) |

4 of 6 done (2 FIXED, 2 confirmed with tests); 2 waiting on a decision.

## Commits

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| a754233 | G5 | Add regression tests for the base features folder |
| a075961 | G13 | Record the existing regression tests as evidence |
| c11d02b | G12 | Count remaining visits in the removal audit |
| 1a06062 | M11 | Record GRID_CLEAN drops in the removal audit |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/grid_clean_preprocess.py`, `src/core/stages/preprocessing.py`** (M11): the GRID_CLEAN entry points take an optional `tracker`, and the stage passes its own. Rows kept and dropped are unchanged; only audit records are added. Without a tracker, behaviour is exactly as before.
2. **`src/core/removal_audit.py`** (G12): one new field on `RemovalEvent`, one new column in the events table, pivot and set summary. Audit output only.
3. **Docs:** `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` (G5, G12, G13, M11 rows).
4. **Tests:** 2 new files, 1 extended.

## Test evidence

**Test cases per finding (10 new cases):**

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G5 | 2 | `test_v2_pipeline_run.py` | new run (and reloaded) has no base `features/` folder; old-layout run still resolves its features from `<run>/features` | New-run test fails on 0df6cd8^ (folder still created). Old-run test passes both times: it pins that old runs keep loading |
| G13 | 0 new | `test_v2_pipeline_run.py` (existing: `test_child_runs_record_their_own_commit_and_branch`, branch-capture test) | base, feature and model runs each record their own commit + branch on manifest and tracker | Existing child-run test fails on 0df6cd8^ with `KeyError: 'identity'`, so it already catches the defect |
| G12 | 5 | `test_removal_audit_visits.py` | event counts valid patient × visit pairs; count reaches events table and pivot; `None` without a visit column; `n_visits` per set; `n_visits` for files dropped before features | All 5 red |
| M11 | 3 | `test_grid_clean_drop_audit.py` | each of the 3 drop steps recorded with its reason and counts; no event when a step drops nothing; without a tracker the output is unchanged | 2 red (the recording tests); the no-tracker case passes both times |
| **Total** | **10** | | | Each fixed finding has **at least one** test that failed before its change |

How the pre-fix checks were done (G5, G13): the test file also imports functions that don't exist before 0df6cd8, so I ran just those tests from a temporary file against `v2_pipeline_run.py` at 0df6cd8^, then restored the file and deleted the temporary test.

**Full suite:**

| | Passed | Failed | xfailed | Collection errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| After W1 | 427 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| W2 review | **437** (+10) | 3 (same) | 6 (same) | 1 (same) |

- **Invariants** (`tests/invariants`): 18 passed, 6 xfailed (SW-568). No XPASS.
- **System** (`tests/system`, synthetic end-to-end runs): 8 passed. The 1 baseline failure (`test_unused_study_group_is_left_out[NOT_LC-L-RAD]`) is unchanged.
- **Synthetic run, outputs checked:** one system run's directory, inspected after the run:
  - base, feature and model run manifests: `git_commit` 1a06062, `git_branch` `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings`;
  - tracker `git` section: same pair;
  - no base `features/` folder;
  - `n_remaining_visits` filled on all 6 tracker events.
  - GRID_CLEAN is off in the synthetic config, so its drop events don't appear in this run. A stage run with GRID_CLEAN enabled comes with the GRID_CLEAN fixes (G10/H4); until then, M11 is proven by the unit tests.

## Metric comparison
Not needed. W2 changes audit and provenance output only; no row, draw, threshold or prediction changes.

## Decisions I made (please check)
1. **G13: no new test.** The tests that came with the fix already cover base, feature and model runs, and they fail on the pre-fix code. Writing another would duplicate them.
2. **G5: one of the two tests passes before and after on purpose.** It pins that old-layout runs keep loading, which the fix had to preserve.
3. **M11: drops matched on `file_write_time` + `device_channel`.** The GRID_CLEAN steps renumber rows, so the tracker's usual index-based `record_filter` can't find what was dropped. Without those two columns, only counts are recorded.
4. **G12: `set_summary` counts visits over all rows in a set,** the same way it already counts patients and files there. Removal events count only VALID rows, matching their existing patient and file counts.
5. **G18 and L13 are not implemented.** Both need a decision I shouldn't guess (questions below).

## Follow-up Jira tickets created
None.

## Questions for Tram
1. **G18 (for Gilad):** what should "a holdout should start only at feature selection" change?
   - `docs/HOLDOUT_TRAINING.md` says `holdout --config` (new run) runs preprocessing → clustering → features → holdout **by design**. A new run has to build the shared stages once.
   - `holdout --run-dir` already starts at the holdout stage and keeps the shared stages frozen (overlay added in 80c600b, 2026-11-01, before G18 was written on 2026-11-05).
   - **My reading:** for a holdout run, the `features` stage should only *extract* features and skip its whole-pool *selection*, since each holdout selects again on its own training patients. That saves time and removes a selection result nobody uses. Is that what Gilad meant?
2. **L13 (for Gilad/Avichai):** should `processed.pkl` keep the site-period / blocked-unit excluded rows (`retain_excluded_override_rows: true`, like the notebook did), or keep the current default (`false`; the rows are still recorded in the removal audit, just not saved in `processed.pkl`)? If the default stays, I'll mark L13 WONTFIX (by design) with that reason.
3. **Pending from W1:** L1 (validation draw rounding), also for Gilad.

## How to review
```bash
git log --oneline sw589-W2-start..sw589-W2-review
git diff --stat sw589-W2-start..sw589-W2-review
git diff sw589-W2-start..sw589-W2-review -- src/core/grid_clean_preprocess.py src/core/stages/preprocessing.py   # riskiest
git show <hash>                                                                                                   # one finding
```
The quickest read is the G5, G12, G13 and M11 rows in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`.

"""Row-retention controls for persisted preprocessing outputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

from src.core.override_scheme import (
    INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_PERIOD,
    INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_UNIT_NUMBER,
)

EXPLICIT_EXCLUSION_REASONS = frozenset(
    {
        INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_PERIOD,
        INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_UNIT_NUMBER,
    }
)

def materialize_processed_for_persistence(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    retain_excluded_override_rows: bool = False,
    retain_invalid_sensor_rows: bool = True,
    retain_aux_index_rows: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Return a full-column copy of ``frame`` filtered for on-disk persistence.

    Column pruning is intentionally not performed. The persisted artifact keeps
    every preprocessing output column for the requested rows.
    """
    persisted = frame.copy()
    if not retain_excluded_override_rows:
        persisted = persisted.loc[
            ~persisted["aggregated_reason"].isin(EXPLICIT_EXCLUSION_REASONS)
        ].copy()
    if not retain_invalid_sensor_rows:
        is_sensor = persisted["channel_type"].eq("SENSOR")
        is_valid = persisted["aggregated_reason"].eq("VALID")
        persisted = persisted.loc[(~is_sensor) | is_valid].copy()
    if not retain_aux_index_rows:
        persisted = persisted.loc[
            ~persisted["channel_type"].isin({"AUX", "INDEX"})
        ].copy()

    return persisted.reset_index(drop=True)


def processed_persistence_from_config(preprocessing: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Resolve preprocessing persistence settings from config mapping."""
    persistence = preprocessing.get("persistence") or {}
    if not isinstance(persistence, dict):
        raise ValueError("preprocessing.persistence must be a mapping")
    return {
        "save_processed": bool(persistence.get("save_processed", True)),
        "save_tracker": bool(persistence.get("save_tracker", True)),

"""Row-retention controls for persisted preprocessing outputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

from src.core.override_scheme import (
    INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_PERIOD,
    INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_UNIT_NUMBER,
)

EXPLICIT_EXCLUSION_REASONS = frozenset(
    {
        INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_PERIOD,
        INVALID_OVERRIDE_BY_UNIT_NUMBER,
    }
)

def materialize_processed_for_persistence(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    retain_excluded_override_rows: bool = False,
    retain_invalid_sensor_rows: bool = True,
    retain_aux_index_rows: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Return a full-column copy of ``frame`` filtered for on-disk persistence.

    Column pruning is intentionally not performed. The persisted artifact keeps
    every preprocessing output column for the requested rows.
    """
    persisted = frame.copy()
    if not retain_excluded_override_rows:
        persisted = persisted.loc[
            ~persisted["aggregated_reason"].isin(EXPLICIT_EXCLUSION_REASONS)
        ].copy()
    if not retain_invalid_sensor_rows:
        is_sensor = persisted["channel_type"].eq("SENSOR")
        is_valid = persisted["aggregated_reason"].eq("VALID")
        persisted = persisted.loc[(~is_sensor) | is_valid].copy()
    if not retain_aux_index_rows:
        persisted = persisted.loc[
            ~persisted["channel_type"].isin({"AUX", "INDEX"})
        ].copy()

    return persisted.reset_index(drop=True)

content.text:
Yes, that's correct, and the code confirms it:

- **What the setting does:** `preprocessing.persistence.retain_excluded_override_rows` only controls what gets **saved** to `processed.pkl`. With `false` (the current default), rows marked `INVALID_overide_by_period` (site-period exclusion) or `INVALID_overide_by_unit_number` (blocked unit) are left out of the saved file (`src/core/preprocessing_persistence.py:35`). With `true`, they're saved, which matches the old notebook.
- **They're in the audit either way.** The override step records them with `tracker.record_filter` when it marks them (`src/core/override_scheme.py:407, 504`), so they appear in the removal audit whatever the setting is.
- **Training is unaffected either way.** These rows are marked invalid, so they never reach training. The choice only matters for anything that reads `processed.pkl` later, such as reports or diagnostics that want to show which traces were excluded and why.

So the question for Gilad/Avichai is: **should `processed.pkl` include the explicitly excluded rows (`true`, as in the notebook), or leave them out (`false`, current default), given that the removal audit records them in both cases?**
- If they say `true`: change the default and add a test.
- If they say `false`: mark L13 WONTFIX (by design), with the reason above.

lastPrompt: I think what is currently stated in G18 is clear. And I think your reading is correct.

content.text:
Your reading and mine agree. Before I write code, you should know the change is bigger than the one-line CLI fix the W0 note suggested.

**What the holdout stage uses from the features stage:** only `features_all.pkl` (the extracted features) and `feature_columns.json` (the candidate columns). Everything the features stage computes *after* extraction is never read by a holdout run:
- the blind split,
- the whole-pool selection,
- the selector,
- the train / test / estimation sets,
- the stability check.

`features_all` is saved unchanged by those later steps. So skipping them can't change holdout results; it just stops doing work nobody uses.

**What has to change:**
1. **Features stage:** add an "extract only" mode. It writes `features_all.pkl`, `features_all_invalid.pkl`, `feature_columns.json`, the tracker and the manifest (marked `extract_only`), and skips the steps listed above.
2. **Pipeline runner:** when the plan runs holdout without training (the `holdout` command), run the features stage in extract-only mode. Its required-artifacts check must accept the smaller output.
3. **`resolve_feature_run`:** today it only treats a feature run as complete if `train_validation_set.pkl` exists. It must accept an extract-only run for holdout. Training on an extract-only run should fail with a clear message instead.
4. **Feature run name:** today it encodes `n_features`, the selection method and the test %. Those would be misleading for an extract-only run, so it gets an `_extract` tag instead.

**How I'd prove it:**
- **Parity test:** the same synthetic data run through holdout with and without the whole-pool selection gives **identical holdout results**.
- **Plan test:** the `holdout` command's plan runs features in extract-only mode and writes no selection artifacts.
- **Training guard:** training on an extract-only run stops with a clear error.
- **Full suite:** passes, with existing holdout and features tests unchanged.

**Model numbers:** unchanged (the parity test proves it). Holdout runs just get faster.

**Risk:** this touches the features stage, the runner and run resolution. All of those are on the training path, so the full suite and system runs will matter.

It goes into W2 as Round 2, on its own commit(s), and I'll update the plan first. Should I go ahead?

message.content: Go ahead

def run_pipeline(options: RunnerOptions) -> PipelineExecutionResult:
    """Execute an ordered, resumable Pipeline V2 stage plan."""
    config, run, clinical_paths = prepare_run_context(options)
    plan = resolve_stage_plan(options, config)
    if options.dry_run:
        return PipelineExecutionResult(
            config=config,
            run=run,
            planned_stages=tuple(plan),
            stages=(),
        )
    if run is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Pipeline run was not prepared")

    executed: list[StageExecutionResult] = []
    prior_results: dict[str, Any] = {}
    completed = list(
        (run.extra.get("resume") or {}).get("completed_stages") or []
    )
    update_resume_state(
        run,
        requested_from_stage=options.from_stage or (plan[0] if plan else None),
    )
    for stage in plan:
        if should_skip_stage(
            run,
            stage,
            resume=options.resume,
            force=options.force,
        ):
            executed.append(StageExecutionResult(stage, "skipped"))
            if stage not in completed:
                completed.append(stage)
            continue
        result = run_single_stage(
            stage,
            run,
            config,
            clinical_paths=clinical_paths,
            prior_results=prior_results,
            holdout_jobs=options.holdout_jobs,
        )
        prior_results[stage] = result
        status = "skipped" if getattr(result, "skipped", False) else "completed"
        executed.append(StageExecutionResult(stage, status, result))
        if status == "completed" and stage not in completed:
            completed.append(stage)
        _record_resume_artifacts(run, completed)
    return PipelineExecutionResult(
        config=config,
        run=run,
        planned_stages=tuple(plan),
        stages=tuple(executed),
    )

def test_trace_rows_split_valid_sensor_channels_and_reject_repeated_keys():
    processed = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "file_write_time": ["t1", "t1", "t1", "t1"],
            "patient_id": ["p1"] * 4,
            "device_channel": ["ch1", "ch2", "ch3", "aux1"],

            "sensor_type": ["type_1"] * 4,
            "aggregated_reason": ["VALID", "VALID", "INVALID_x", "VALID"],
            "normalized_resampled_signals": [[1.0], [2.0], [3.0], [4.0]],
            "raw_signal": [[0]] * 4,
        }
    )
    valid, invalid = trace_rows_for_features(
        processed, signal_column="normalized_resampled_signals"

        assert "repeat" in str(exc)

def _patch_feature_algorithms(monkeypatch):
    def extract(data, **kwargs):
        feature_frame = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "feature_one": range(1, len(data) + 1),
                "feature_two": range(11, 11 + len(data)),
            },
            index=data.index,
        )
        return (
            pd.concat(
                [data.reset_index(drop=True), feature_frame.reset_index(drop=True)],
                axis=1,
            ),
            feature_frame.reset_index(drop=True),
        )

    def select(data, features_df, **kwargs):
        selected = features_df[["feature_one"]].copy()
        return pd.concat([data.reset_index(drop=True), selected], axis=1), selected

    def fit(features_df, target, **kwargs):
        return FeatureSelectorState(feature_names=["feature_two"])

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "src.core.stages.features.extract_sectional_features",
        extract,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr("src.core.stages.features.select_features", select)
    monkeypatch.setattr("src.core.stages.features.fit_selector", fit)


def test_run_features_builds_train_and_estimation_sets(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    _patch_feature_algorithms(monkeypatch)
    valid, invalid = _clustered_rows()
    run = _run(tmp_path)
    tracker = Tracker()
    tracker.config["cluster"] = {"enabled": True}

    result = run_features(
        run,
        config={},
        clustered=valid,
        clustered_invalid=invalid,
        tracker=tracker,
        settings=FeaturesSettings(upload_audit=False),
    )

    assert result.selected_feature_names == ["feature_one"]
    assert result.selector_state.feature_names == ["feature_one"]
    assert len(result.train_validation_set) == 2
    assert result.test_set.empty
    assert len(result.features_all) == 3
    assert set(result.features_all["sensor_type"]) == {"type_2", "type_3"}
    assert len(result.estimation_pickle) == 2
    assert set(result.estimation_pickle["file_write_time"]) == {"t3", "t4"}
    assert set(result.train_validation_set["binary_study_group"]) == {1, 2}
    assert "INVALID_electric" in set(result.estimation_pickle["aggregated_reason"])
    assert "NOT_IN_TRAIN_VAL_TEST_DATA" in set(
        result.estimation_pickle["aggregated_reason"]
    )
    assert result.features_all_path and result.features_all_path.is_file()
    assert result.selector_path and result.selector_path.is_file()
    assert result.feature_run is not None
    assert result.feature_run.feature_run_path.parent.name == "feature_runs"

    manifest = json.loads((run.run_path / "manifest.json").read_text())
    assert manifest["stages"]["features"]["status"] == "completed"
    assert manifest["feature_runs"][0]["selected_feature_count"] == 1
    assert manifest["feature_runs"][0]["path"].startswith("feature_runs/")

    feature_manifest = json.loads(
        (result.feature_run.feature_run_path / "manifest.json").read_text()
    )
    assert feature_manifest["patient_splits"]["train_validation"] == {
        "rows": 2,
        "patients": 2,
        "patients_by_study_group": {"LC": 1, "NOT_LC": 1},
    }
    assert feature_manifest["patient_splits"]["blind_test"]["patients"] == 0
    assert feature_manifest["feature_selection"]["selected_feature_count"] == 1
    assert (
        result.feature_run.feature_run_path / "resolved_feature_config.yaml"
